name: modernization-pipeline
description: Repeatable delivery pipeline: an MS Access or Excel VBA app becomes a Django app that is proven to behave the same. Each stage is one run of .claude/workflows/run-stage.js for one engagement, started by the orchestrating session after the environment preflight and the stage's prepare list, through a per-stage launcher that .claude/workflows/make-launcher.py writes with pipeline.json (sliced), engagement.json and gates.json embedded (docs/runbook.md 2(f)). The first engagements (the public demos) run in bootstrap mode and build the tools; later engagements reuse them.
_status: Proposal v2, reviewed 2026-10-16. Nothing here has been run. Read docs/proposal.md, docs/contracts.md and docs/runbook.md first.

demo.name: access-excel-to-django
demo.visibility: private until the northwind-demo S6 gate, then public

client.name: <client-slug>-<app-slug>
client.visibility: private, owned by the client; created by the client before the first stage that pushes code. Health-check and assessment engagements use target.mode local instead.

records.name: $HOME/engagements/<id>/record (clients); demos keep records in engagements/<id>
records.visibility: a local git repo per client, never pushed to GitHub, never in the pipeline repo, never in a cloud session

item_ids._rule: Fan-out item ids (S1 areas, S5 features) become Django app labels and test module names: they match the pattern, are not reserved, differ from the app slug and are unique.

care-plan._note: No pipeline stage yet; care-plan work is an open question in proposal §12.

pricing_tiers.scope: inventory, keep/drop list, rules spec, fixed quote; credited toward the migration
move tables to Postgres or SQL Server, re-link the Access screens, backups
1 app, up to about 20 forms and reports

pricing.rule: price_usd = ceil(hours x rate / round_to_usd) x round_to_usd for each of low, point and high, where rate is engagement commercial.rate_usd_per_hour when set, else rate_usd_per_hour; the quoted point is clamped to the tier row's price_usd range and the quote states any clamp
pricing._source: business plan §7: at least 130 USD/h by project 5; first projects may set commercial.rate_usd_per_hour to 60-90

_environment: The orchestrator runs this list before every stage, in this order. An item applies to a stage when its stages include the stage, its kinds (if any) include the engagement's source kind, and its when (if any) exits 0. For each item it runs check; if check fails, fix and check again; it stops on failure unless the item is optional. This list is the only source: stages have no preflight lists. Its commands are exempt from the one-line rule for agent commands. The dry run returns the applying items in this order, filled with the engagement's paths but never wrapped: these commands need Docker and data.env, so the orchestrator runs them directly in demo sessions and in a plain terminal outside Claude for client engagements, never through mp-run or an agent.

environment.check: F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && D=$HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && test -f "$F" && test -f "$D" && test "$(stat -c %a "$F")" = 600 && test "$(stat -c %a "$D")" = 600 && grep -q '^export PATH=' "$F" && grep -q '^export UV_TOOL_DIR=' "$F" && test -z "$(grep -v '^export [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=' "$F" "$D")"
environment.fix: mkdir -p $HOME/.config/modernization && F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && D=$HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && umask 077 && touch "$F" "$D" && chmod 600 "$F" "$D" && { grep -v '^export PATH=' "$F"; echo "export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:\$PATH"; } > "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F" && { grep -v '^export UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=' "$F"; echo 'export UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed'; } > "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F" && { grep -v '^export UV_TOOL_DIR=' "$F"; echo "export UV_TOOL_DIR=$HOME/.cache/uv-tools"; } > "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F"
environment.note: Runs first. Creates two files, both chmod 600 and holding only `export NAME=value` lines with absolute values. The env file ($HOME/.config/modernization/env) has no secrets: mp-run and mp-data source it before every command, so agents see it; the mp_agent logins in its PG_URL and MSSQL_URL are refused by every mpdata_ database. data.env ($HOME/.config/modernization/data.env) holds every secret value (the database superuser and mp_runner URLs, the SQL Server sa password, and the variables that `env:NAME` secret refs name); only mp-data and the operator read it, mp-run makes it unreadable and mp-data hides it from its toolkit child. Every later check and fix sources what it needs. UV_TOOL_DIR points uvx at a writable tool directory ($HOME/.cache/uv-tools), because mp-run mounts $HOME/.local/share/uv read-only.

environment.fix: mkdir -p $HOME/.local/share/modernization $HOME/.local/bin && python3 -m venv $HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-venv && $HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-venv/bin/pip install uv==0.13.1 && ln -sf $HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-venv/bin/uv $HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-venv/bin/uvx $HOME/.local/bin/

environment.fix: mkdir -p $HOME/.local/bin && d=$(mktemp -d) && curl -fsSL -o "$d/jq" https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.8.1/jq-linux-amd64 && echo "020468de7539ce70ef1bceaf7cde2e8c4f2ca6c3afb84642aabc5c97d9fc2a0d  $d/jq" | sha256sum -c - && test "$(stat -c %s "$d/jq")" = 2255816 && chmod 755 "$d/jq" && mv "$d/jq" $HOME/.local/bin/jq && rm -rf "$d"
environment.note: Right after uv because later items use it (the mssql `when`). S1, S4, S5 and S6 commands, test_rules.py and the orchestrator's items_from need jq 1.7 or 1.8; the check accepts one already on PATH. The fix installs the static jq 1.8.1 binary pinned in stack.jq into $HOME/.local/bin, which the env file puts first on PATH. jq 1.8.1 is present here.
The container ships Python 3.14.4 only; the toolkit and the cookiecutter-django app need ==3.13.*. UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed keeps uv on the managed build.

No fix: stop and ask. Rootless Docker 29.8 works here. It runs the database containers from S3 on and is checked every stage so a missing daemon shows up early. Agent commands that run through mp-run cannot reach it (mp-run hides the Docker sockets and unsets DOCKER_HOST), and neither can the toolkit child of a data-plane call; only an S0 run in bootstrap mode, which uses the braced form, can.

environment.check: gh auth status --hostname github.com >/dev/null 2>&1 && gh auth status --hostname github.com 2>&1 | grep -q 'Logged in to github\.com .*/hosts\.yml)' && git -C {{p.pipeline}} remote get-url origin | grep -q '^https://github\.com/' && { jq -e '.bootstrap != true' {{p.records}}/engagement.json >/dev/null || git -C {{p.target_repo}} remote get-url origin | grep -q '^https://github\.com/'; } && git config --global --get-all credential.https://github.com.helper | grep -q 'gh auth git-credential'
environment.note: No fix: stop and ask the user to log in with gh's file-stored token: `gh auth login --insecure-storage` (on a client host, a fine-grained token limited to the pipeline repo: `gh auth login --with-token --insecure-storage` with the token on stdin; docs/runbook.md 1.6). Log in choosing HTTPS, then run `gh config set git_protocol https` and `gh auth setup-git`, so git pushes with the same token. mp-run hides $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and with it the system keyring, so git and gh inside mp-run (integrate and checkpoint pushes, pipeline PRs) work only with a token in gh's hosts.yml; the check proves that `gh auth status` names hosts.yml, that the pipeline clone's origin (and a demo's target clone's origin) is an https://github.com/ URL, and that gh is git's credential helper for github.com. mp-run hides ssh-agent, so an SSH origin (what `gh repo create --clone` makes when git_protocol is ssh) cannot push from integrate or checkpoint; fix one with `git -C <repo> remote set-url origin https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git`. This login pushes and opens PRs for the pipeline repo (which holds the demo records) and the demo repo; a client records repo is never pushed. A client target repo never uses it: integrate pushes with `mp-data push` and handles PRs with `mp-data gh`, both with the token from the engagement's secrets.github_push.ref.

No fix (needs sudo): stop and ask. Every stage and engagement needs bubblewrap: the driver runs every agent command through mp-run from S1 on (and in S0 for client engagements), mp-data runs its toolkit child under bwrap in every stage, and S0.workspace's mp-run tests use it. Install with `sudo apt-get install bubblewrap`. On Ubuntu 24.04 and later, if the check still fails and `sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` prints 1, bwrap needs an AppArmor profile named bwrap that allows user namespaces. Look for one first: `grep -l '^profile bwrap ' /etc/apparmor.d/*`. Ubuntu 26.04 ships it in /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict (package apparmor); reload it with `sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict`. Only when no file defines it, write /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap with the profile from the Claude Code sandboxing docs (lines `abi <abi/4.0>,`, `include <tunables/global>`, `profile bwrap /usr/bin/bwrap flags=(unconfined) {`, `  userns,`, `  include if exists <local/bwrap>`, `}`) and run `sudo systemctl reload apparmor`. Never define a second profile named bwrap: it would replace the stock one. Measured here: bubblewrap 0.11.1, Ubuntu 26.04 with /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict, the restriction is on (1) and the check passes. socat is not needed: client sessions do not use the Claude Code sandbox.

environment.fix: d=$(mktemp -d) && (cd "$d" && apt-get download libodbc2 libltdl7 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0) && mkdir -p $HOME/.local/share/modernization/syslibs && for f in "$d"/*.deb; do dpkg -x "$f" $HOME/.local/share/modernization/syslibs; done && rm -rf "$d" && F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && umask 077 && { grep -v '^export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=' "$F"; echo "export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/syslibs/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu"; } > "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F"

environment.check: F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && D=$HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && test "$(stat -c %a "$D")" = 600 && grep -qx 'export PG_URL=postgresql://mp_agent:mp-agent@127.0.0.1:55432' "$F" && pw=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_DATA_PG_URL=postgresql://postgres:\([0-9a-f]*\)@127\.0\.0\.1:55432$|\1|p' "$D") && test -n "$pw" && rp=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_RUNNER_PG_URL=postgresql://mp_runner:\([0-9a-f]*\)@127\.0\.0\.1:55432$|\1|p' "$D") && test -n "$rp" && docker exec mp-pg16 pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -q && test "$(docker exec mp-pg16 sh -c 'head -n 5 "$PGDATA/pg_hba.conf"')" = "$(printf '%s\n' 'host /^mpdata_ mp_agent all reject' 'host postgres,/^mpdata_ mp_runner all scram-sha-256' 'host all mp_runner all reject' 'host all all 127.0.0.1/32 scram-sha-256' 'host all all ::1/128 scram-sha-256')" && PGPASSWORD=$pw docker exec -e PGPASSWORD mp-pg16 psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -d postgres -qAtc "select 1 from pg_database where datname = 'mpdata_probe'" | grep -qx 1 && docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=mp-agent mp-pg16 psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U mp_agent -d postgres -qAtc 'select rolcreatedb and not rolsuper and not rolcreaterole from pg_roles where rolname = current_user' | grep -qx t && docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=mp-agent mp-pg16 psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U mp_agent -d mpdata_probe -qAtc 'select 1' 2>&1 | grep -q 'pg_hba.conf rejects connection' && PGPASSWORD=$rp docker exec -e PGPASSWORD mp-pg16 psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U mp_runner -d mpdata_probe -qAtc 'select rolcreatedb and not rolsuper and not rolcreaterole from pg_roles where rolname = current_user' | grep -qx t && PGPASSWORD=$rp docker exec -e PGPASSWORD mp-pg16 psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U mp_runner -d template1 -qAtc 'select 1' 2>&1 | grep -q 'pg_hba.conf rejects connection'
environment.note: Docker container mp-pg16 on 127.0.0.1:55432 with a named volume. This item is the only place that provisions PostgreSQL; scripts/dev_db.sh only creates and drops agent databases as mp_agent. Three roles. The superuser password is generated once (hex), kept only in data.env as MP_DATA_PG_URL and set with ALTER ROLE over the container's local socket on every fix, so the fix also repairs a volume created with another password or a lost data.env. Agents get PG_URL in the env file: role mp_agent, LOGIN CREATEDB, password mp-agent. Role mp_runner (LOGIN CREATEDB, generated hex password, MP_RUNNER_PG_URL in data.env only) is the login mp-data gives to commands that run agent-written code. The fix keeps five lines at the top of pg_hba.conf, in this order: `host /^mpdata_ mp_agent all reject`, `host postgres,/^mpdata_ mp_runner all scram-sha-256` and `host all mp_runner all reject` (PostgreSQL 16 reads a database entry that starts with / as a regular expression, so mp_agent never reaches an mpdata_ database and mp_runner reaches only those and the postgres maintenance database), then scram-sha-256 for 127.0.0.1/32 and ::1/128, which initdb's defaults trust inside the container. It reloads the configuration and proves that pg_hba_file_rules reports no error. The check proves that these five lines lead pg_hba.conf, that all three passwords work, that mp_agent is rejected from database mpdata_probe (created by the superuser), and that mp_runner reaches mpdata_probe but is rejected from template1. Databases: stack.database_urls.names. No Unix-socket URLs. The wait loop polls without sleep and waits for TCP, which the image opens only after its first-start initialisation.

environment.check: F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && D=$HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && test "$(stat -c %a "$D")" = 600 && test -z "$(grep '^export MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=' "$F")" && sa=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)$|\1|p' "$D") && test -n "$sa" && grep -qxF "export MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL=mssql://sa:$sa@127.0.0.1:14330" "$D" && rp=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL=mssql://mp_runner:\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)@127\.0\.0\.1:14330$|\1|p' "$D") && test -n "$rp" && ap=$(sed -n 's|^export MSSQL_URL=mssql://mp_agent:\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)@127\.0\.0\.1:14330$|\1|p' "$F") && test -n "$ap" && SQLCMDPASSWORD=$sa docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U sa -b -h -1 -W -Q "set nocount on; select count(*) from sys.databases where name = 'mpdata_probe'" | grep -qx 1 && SQLCMDPASSWORD=$ap docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U mp_agent -b -h -1 -W -Q "set nocount on; select concat(has_perms_by_name(null, null, 'CREATE ANY DATABASE'), is_srvrolemember('dbcreator'), is_srvrolemember('sysadmin'))" | grep -qx 100 && SQLCMDPASSWORD=$rp docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U mp_runner -b -h -1 -W -Q "set nocount on; select concat(has_perms_by_name(null, null, 'CREATE ANY DATABASE'), is_srvrolemember('dbcreator'), is_srvrolemember('sysadmin'))" | grep -qx 100 && SQLCMDPASSWORD=$ap docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U mp_agent -d mpdata_probe -b -Q 'select 1' 2>&1 | grep -q 'Cannot open database'
environment.fix: F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && D=$HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && umask 077 && touch "$D" && chmod 600 "$D" && sa=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)$|\1|p' "$D") && { test -n "$sa" || sa=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)$|\1|p' "$F"); } && { test -n "$sa" || sa=$(openssl rand -hex 16)Aa1-; } && rp=$(sed -n 's|^export MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL=mssql://mp_runner:\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)@127\.0\.0\.1:14330$|\1|p' "$D") && { test -n "$rp" || rp=$(openssl rand -hex 16)Aa1-; } && { grep -Ev '^export (MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD|MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL|MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL)=' "$D"; echo "export MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=$sa"; echo "export MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL=mssql://sa:$sa@127.0.0.1:14330"; echo "export MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL=mssql://mp_runner:$rp@127.0.0.1:14330"; } > "$D.new" && mv "$D.new" "$D" && (docker start mp-mssql22 2>/dev/null || MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=$sa docker run -d --name mp-mssql22 --restart unless-stopped -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e MSSQL_PID=Developer -e MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD -p 127.0.0.1:14330:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest@sha256:cf8f0ab2ebe61feec2eed2629061a07d247f791c2a8ddda74a4ac9f06a291718) && SQLCMDPASSWORD=$sa timeout 180 sh -c 'until docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U sa -Q "select 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do :; done' && ap=$(sed -n 's|^export MSSQL_URL=mssql://mp_agent:\([A-Za-z0-9-]*\)@127\.0\.0\.1:14330$|\1|p' "$F") && { test -n "$ap" || ap=$(openssl rand -hex 16)Aa1-; } && printf '%s\n' "if suser_id('mp_agent') is null begin create login mp_agent with password = '$ap'; end else begin alter login mp_agent with password = '$ap'; end; if suser_id('mp_runner') is null begin create login mp_runner with password = '$rp'; end else begin alter login mp_runner with password = '$rp'; end; grant create any database to mp_agent; grant create any database to mp_runner; if is_srvrolemember('dbcreator', 'mp_agent') = 1 alter server role dbcreator drop member mp_agent; if is_srvrolemember('dbcreator', 'mp_runner') = 1 alter server role dbcreator drop member mp_runner; if db_id('mpdata_probe') is null create database mpdata_probe;" go | SQLCMDPASSWORD=$sa docker exec -i -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U sa -b && { grep -Ev '^export (MSSQL_URL|MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD)=' "$F"; echo "export MSSQL_URL=mssql://mp_agent:$ap@127.0.0.1:14330"; } > "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F"
environment.note: Applies only when the `when` command exits 0 (mssql is database.primary or in database.verify_also). Container mp-mssql22 (Developer edition: dev and test only) on 127.0.0.1:14330. This item is the only place that provisions SQL Server. Every password here (sa, mp_agent, mp_runner) is generated once as `$(openssl rand -hex 16)Aa1-` (URL-safe, and it meets the SQL Server password policy) and never printed or put on a command line: sqlcmd gets the login password through SQLCMDPASSWORD, and the statements that set the mp_agent and mp_runner passwords on stdin, as the postgres fix does with psql. The sa password lives only in data.env, as MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD and MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL; an MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD line that an earlier fix left in the env file is reused, moved to data.env and removed from the env file. Agents get MSSQL_URL in the env file: login mp_agent with GRANT CREATE ANY DATABASE (not dbcreator). Login mp_runner has the same rights and its URL only in data.env (MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL); mp-data gives it to commands that run agent-written code. A new database maps only its creator (as dbo), so mp_agent cannot open the mpdata_ databases that sa or mp_runner create; the check proves that on database mpdata_probe. If data.env was lost while the container kept the old sa password, run `docker rm -f mp-mssql22` and fix again (the container has no volume; every database in it can be rebuilt).

environment.check: . $HOME/.config/modernization/env && B=$HOME/.local/bin && test "$(command -v mp-data)" = "$B/mp-data" && test "$(command -v mp-run)" = "$B/mp-run" && test "$(stat -c '%F %a' "$B/mp-data" "$B/mp-run" "$B/mp-bash-hook")" = "$(printf 'regular file 755\n%.0s' 1 2 3)" && { jq -e '.bootstrap == true' {{p.records}}/engagement.json >/dev/null || { P=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit.pin && test -s "$P" && R=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit@$(cat "$P") && cmp -s "$R/scripts/mp-data" "$B/mp-data" && cmp -s "$R/scripts/mp-run" "$B/mp-run" && cmp -s "$R/scripts/mp-bash-hook" "$B/mp-bash-hook"; }; }
environment.fix: . $HOME/.config/modernization/env && P=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit.pin && if jq -e '.bootstrap == true' {{p.records}}/engagement.json >/dev/null || test ! -s "$P"; then {{p.pipeline}}/scripts/install-mp-data.sh; else "$HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit@$(cat "$P")/scripts/install-mp-data.sh"; fi
environment.note: Applies once S0 has merged (skipped in the first S0 bootstrap, which builds the scripts). scripts/install-mp-data.sh copies scripts/mp-data, scripts/mp-run and scripts/mp-bash-hook from its own checkout into $HOME/.local/bin as mode-755 copies, never symlinks, so agents cannot edit the copies that run: mp-run binds $HOME/.local/bin read-only and client settings deny edits there. The check proves that, after sourcing the env file, the bare words mp-data and mp-run resolve to those copies and that all three are regular files with mode 755. Demos (bootstrap true) install from the pipeline checkout; after a merge that changes one of the three scripts, run the fix again from an up-to-date main checkout. Client engagements (bootstrap false) run a reviewed release: the operator pins it once per host with `mp-data pin <sha>` in a terminal, from a pipeline clone whose origin/main holds that sha; pin checks the release out at $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit@<sha> and installs that release's scripts. For them the check also needs a pin ($HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit.pin, which `mp-data pin --status` reports) and installed copies equal to the pinned release's scripts, and the fix reinstalls from the pinned release. Without a pin the fix installs from the pipeline checkout and the check still fails: pin, then check again.

environment.check: test -x "$(git -C {{p.pipeline}} rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks/pre-commit)" && p=$(sed -n 's/^INSTALL_PYTHON=//p' "$(git -C {{p.pipeline}} rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks/pre-commit)" | tr -d "'") && test -x "$p" && { test ! -f {{p.target_repo}}/.pre-commit-config.yaml || { h=$(git -C {{p.target_repo}} rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks/pre-commit) && test -x "$h" && q=$(sed -n 's/^INSTALL_PYTHON=//p' "$h" | tr -d "'") && test -x "$q"; }; }
environment.fix: . $HOME/.config/modernization/env && (cd {{p.pipeline}} && uv run pre-commit install) && (cd {{p.target_repo}} && { test ! -f .pre-commit-config.yaml || uv run --project {{p.pipeline}} pre-commit install; })
environment.note: Applies once S0 has merged. Fresh clones have no git hooks, so the forbidden-file hooks would not fire on commit. The target repo gets its hook once it has a .pre-commit-config.yaml. The check asks git for the hook path (--path-format=absolute), because .git is a file in a worktree. A client pipeline is a worktree, so its hook is the shared .git/hooks/pre-commit of $HOME/sourcecode/modernization-pipeline, and pre-commit writes INSTALL_PYTHON=<that worktree>/.venv/bin/python3 into it. After docs/runbook.md section 7 removes that worktree, the hook would fail every later commit (pre-commit is not on PATH inside mp-run); the check tests INSTALL_PYTHON so the fix reinstalls it. The hooks run in the integrate and checkpoint commits, inside mp-run from S1 on. On client repos the operator's own plain-terminal git runs as rgit, with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false` (docs/runbook.md 1.3), because agents can write the pre-commit cache those hooks use.

environment.fix: F=$HOME/.config/modernization/env && umask 077 && { grep -v '^export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=' "$F"; echo "export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=$HOME/.cache/ms-playwright"; } > "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F" && . "$F" && (cd {{p.target}}/app && uv run playwright install chromium)

Optional, no fix (no root here). When soffice is absent, S2.reference_xlsm skips the LibreOffice cross-check and says so in notes.

Manual, once per machine, no fix: stop and ask. In /config raise "Dynamic workflow size" so one workflow may run at least 20 agents, then run `touch $HOME/.config/modernization/workflow-size-raised` and note the setting in log.md. This machine runs 6 agents at a time; larger fan-outs queue.

data_plane._rule: Agents may read the design zone: out/ (scrubbed model and inventory, plus the reference catalog and generated SQL under out/reference/), review/ (reviewer scratch, review/<slot>/) and synthetic/ (artefacts derived only from committed synthetic seeds: synthetic/reference/, synthetic/results/<stage>/, synthetic/results/obtained/, synthetic/media/). Only mp-data reads the data zone. In pipeline.json every mp-data invocation is a data-plane call: one standalone command `mp-data [--if-built] <command> {{p.records}}/engagement.json [args]` with no shell operator, redirection, substitution, subshell, brace group, cd, if or for, and no $ other than the literal $MP_DB_SUFFIX. pipeline.json never writes --slot: the driver emits each call as `mp-data --slot <slot> ...` and replaces $MP_DB_SUFFIX with the slot. Quoted arguments are allowed. Steps that used to be chained with && are separate commands. Every other command that reads a data-zone path is an error; commands that touch only the design zone and committed files run as `uv run toolkit ...` with full output. These measures stop accidental exposure of client data by agents that follow their prompts; they do not claim to contain a deliberately hostile agent (threat model and recorded residual risks: docs/contracts.md §1, docs/proposal.md §11).
data_plane._install: Built by S0.workspace (scripts/mp-data, scripts/mp-run, scripts/mp-bash-hook, scripts/install-mp-data.sh, toolkit/dataplane.py, toolkit/schemas/summary.schema.json) and installed as mode-755 copies in $HOME/.local/bin by environment item mp_data. Global flags come before the command. `--slot <slot>` exports MP_DB_SUFFIX=<slot> (default orchestrator). `--if-built` exits 0 with summary status not-built when the engagement has bootstrap true and toolkit/commands/<command>.py does not exist in the pipeline worktree; with bootstrap false it changes nothing. mp-data sources $HOME/.config/modernization/env and reads $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env without exporting it. Its toolkit root is the pipeline worktree from {{p.records}}/paths.local.json when bootstrap is true; otherwise the reviewed release $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit@<sha> named in $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit.pin (`mp-data pin <sha>`, operator only, in a terminal; `mp-data pin --status` reports it), run with that worktree's .venv and UV_CACHE_DIR=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-cache, both read-only inside mp-run, so agent commands cannot change the code that reads client data. It runs `uv run --project <root> python -m toolkit.dataplane <command> <args>`, which starts `<root>/.venv/bin/toolkit <command>` as a child (no uv inside the jail) under `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --die-with-parent --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc`: everything is read-only except this engagement's data zone (its directories and scrub-map.json), a fresh TMPDIR per call under {{p.private}}/logs/ (removed afterwards, because temporary files can hold engagement values) and the call's declared outputs (the --junit-dir directory and the parent directory of each --out, --report and --matrix path; fetch: the records dir and the toolkit's vendor/; guard: its pre-commit cache $HOME/.local/share/modernization/pre-commit, used as PRE_COMMIT_HOME; golden record: {{p.target}}/goldens/; push and gh: the target repo's git directories; purge: {{p.private}} and the records dir). So a data-plane call writes the design zone only through a declared output: `mp-data reference build --dataset engagement` writes only reference/engagement.accdb (xlsm .xlsx), the seed databases in {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/ are built with `uv run toolkit reference build <eng> --dataset seeds|seed-N`, and `--dataset all` exits 2. The masks come last: tmpfs over every other engagement's private/ and record/ (for every command, purge included), over the pass store and over the directories that hold the operator's session sockets ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, ${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-<uid> and /run/screen/S-<user>, each when present: a read-only mount does not stop connect() on a unix socket); /dev/null over data.env, /var/run/docker.sock and the unix socket DOCKER_HOST names when it lies outside $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. So data.env, the pass store, Docker, the session bus and other engagements are hidden; the host network is kept. Before it starts the child, mp-data resolves exactly the secret refs the command needs (push and gh: secrets.github_push.ref; stage1 `--target-db secret:<ref>`: that ref; the readers of an encrypted source: its password refs) and hands each value to the child only as MP_SECRET_<FIELD> in its environment (the field path upper-cased, each run of characters outside [A-Z0-9] replaced by _, for example MP_SECRET_SECRETS_GITHUB_PUSH_REF), never in argv, a log or a file; inside the jail toolkit/secrets.py reads only those variables. For purge it also sets MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES before the jail starts: the comma-separated db_names of every other engagement.json under $HOME/engagements/*/record/ and {{p.pipeline}}/engagements/ (empty when there is none); purge exits 2 when it is unset. So app code that a data-plane call starts (Django under `equivalence --adapter django`, app-function rewrites under reference and golden) can write only there. A Django cell runs {{p.target}}/app/.venv/bin/python, because there is no uv in the jail; when that interpreter is missing the call exits 2 naming `cd {{p.target}}/app && uv sync --locked`, which S5 and S6 prepare run first. The child gets the env-file variables, MP_QUIET=1, MP_DB_SUFFIX, MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX=mpdata_test_, MP_SANDBOX=mp-data and one URL per local server under both names (MP_DATA_PG_URL and PG_URL, MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL and MSSQL_URL; both unset when data.env lacks that URL): the mp_runner URLs for equivalence, reference build|run|selfcheck and golden record, the superuser URLs for stage1 and purge, and no database URL for any other command. No other data.env value reaches it, apart from the MP_SECRET_ values above. mp-data creates the parent directory of any --out, --report or --matrix path and the --junit-dir directory, and exits 2 for an output path outside the pipeline, target repo, records or private directories. It refuses (exit 2) a literal --target-db URL, a `local:<name>` without the mpdata_ prefix, and loading engagement rows into an mpdata_ database owned by anyone but postgres, sa or mp_runner. `--target-db local:<name>` means database <name> on the local server of each dialect in --dialects; `secret:<ref>` is a client server whose URL mp-data resolves before the jail and hands over as an MP_SECRET_ variable, never printed. `push <eng> --branch <b>` pushes local branch <b> of the target repo to origin <b> through a one-shot credential helper. `gh <eng> -- pr create|view|list|checks|merge ...` and `gh <eng> -- run list|view ...` run the GitHub CLI in the target repo and return gh's stdout lines in the summary's messages. Both take the token from secrets.github_push.ref (MP_SECRET_SECRETS_GITHUB_PUSH_REF in the jail), never print it, and require origin https://github.com/<target.repo>.
data_plane._output: Full stdout and stderr go to {{p.private}}/logs/<utc-ts>-<slot>-<pid>-<command>.log, so parallel calls never share a log. stdout is exactly one JSON summary (toolkit/schemas/summary.schema.json, key names per docs/contracts.md §17, among them counts, cells, units and tables; status ok, failed, error, recorded, no-data or not-built; counts, hashes, column names and unit ids, never values). A summary that contains a corpus string is withheld and replaced by an error summary. The exit code is the toolkit's, except that mp-data exits 2 when the toolkit exited 0 but its summary was missing, invalid or withheld.
data_plane._mp_run: Agents run every other command through `mp-run --eng {{p.records}}/engagement.json --slot <slot> -- '<command>'` (one quoted command string). mp-run reads paths.local.json, sources the env file (never data.env), exports MP_DB_SUFFIX=<slot> and MP_SANDBOX=mp-run, unsets DOCKER_HOST, changes to the pipeline checkout unless the command starts with `cd `, and runs `bash -c` under `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --die-with-parent --dev-bind / / --proc /proc`. Read-only binds come first: $HOME/.local/bin, $HOME/.local/share/modernization, $HOME/.local/share/uv, $HOME/.config/modernization, $HOME/.claude, $HOME/.claude.json, the engagement's client-session.json, the pipeline worktree's .claude/ and .mcp.json, and the git hooks and git config of the pipeline and target repos (each when present). The masks come after them, because a later mount wins in bwrap (a read-only bind of $HOME/.config/modernization placed after the mask over data.env makes data.env readable again): tmpfs over every data-zone directory of this engagement, over every other engagement's private/ and record/, over the pass store (${PASSWORD_STORE_DIR:-$HOME/.password-store}), and over $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (default /run/user/<uid>), ${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-<uid> and /run/screen/S-<user> (each when present: the session bus there reaches the systemd user manager, which starts commands outside mp-run, rootless Docker keeps its socket there, and a read-only mount does not stop connect() on a unix socket); /dev/null over scrub-map.json, data.env, /var/run/docker.sock and the unix socket DOCKER_HOST names when it lies outside $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. With $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR hidden, the keyring, ssh-agent and gpg-agent do not work inside mp-run, so git and gh there use gh's file-stored token (environment item gh). The host network is kept, so the 127.0.0.1 databases work. Its exit code is the command's. Only an S0 run in bootstrap mode, before mp-run exists, uses the braced form `. {{p.env_file}} && export MP_DB_SUFFIX=<slot> && cd {{p.pipeline}} && { <command>; }` (without `cd {{p.pipeline}} && ` when the command starts with `cd `).

stack.python_build: 3.13.16 (uv python install; the container ships Python 3.14.4 only)

jq._why: S1, S4, S5 and S6 commands, test_rules.py and the orchestrator's items_from use jq 1.7 or 1.8. Environment item jq installs this static binary into $HOME/.local/bin when none is on PATH.

stack._django: 5.2 LTS, supported to April 2028. The template pins 5.2.12 and the overlay upgrades it. Plan the move to 6.2 LTS after April 2027.
databases: PostgreSQL 16: Docker container mp-pg16 locally, service container in target CI
SQL Server 2022 / Azure SQL through mssql-django 2.0.0 with the mssql-python driver (OPTIONS python_driver mssql_python): Docker container mp-mssql22 locally, service container in target CI

database_urls._passwords: Generated once by the environment fixes and never printed: the PostgreSQL superuser and mp_runner passwords as `openssl rand -hex 24`; the SQL Server sa, mp_agent and mp_runner passwords as `$(openssl rand -hex 16)Aa1-` (URL-safe, and it meets the SQL Server password policy). The PostgreSQL mp_agent password is the fixed mp-agent: pg_hba.conf, not the password, keeps mp_agent out of mpdata_ databases.
names: mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_stage1 (Stage 1 load of engagement rows: `--target-db local:mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_stage1`, mp-data only, superuser URL)

mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate (engagement rows imported at the S5 client gate by the operator in a plain terminal: created by the superuser and owned by mp_runner, the app connects with the mp_runner URL; dropped once the counts match)
mpdata_test_{{e.db_name}}_<slot> (Django test databases of data-plane equivalence runs, created by mp_runner; mp-data sets MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX=mpdata_test_)
test_{{e.db_name}}_<MP_DB_SUFFIX> (Django test databases of agent runs; the overlay's test-db helper names every test database <MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX>{{e.db_name}}_<MP_DB_SUFFIX>, prefix default test_)
database_urls._rule: Engagement rows only ever enter local databases whose name starts with mpdata_, and only through mp-data or the operator. Each server has three logins. mp_agent (PG_URL and MSSQL_URL in the env file; PostgreSQL LOGIN CREATEDB, SQL Server CREATE ANY DATABASE, not dbcreator) is the agents' login, and every mpdata_ database refuses it: PostgreSQL through the first pg_hba.conf line `host /^mpdata_ mp_agent all reject`, SQL Server because a new database maps only its creator. mp_runner (same rights; MP_RUNNER_PG_URL and MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL) is what mp-data gives to commands that run agent-written code (equivalence, reference build|run|selfcheck, golden record); PostgreSQL admits it only to the postgres database and mpdata_ databases. The superusers postgres and sa (MP_DATA_PG_URL, MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL) serve stage1, purge and the operator's gate set-up (the gate import itself runs the app as mp_runner). The MP_DATA_* and MP_RUNNER_* URLs live only in data.env, which only mp-data and the operator read; inside mp-data the toolkit child sees the chosen URL as both MP_DATA_PG_URL and PG_URL (likewise for SQL Server). mp-data refuses to load engagement rows into an mpdata_ database owned by anyone but postgres, sa or mp_runner, because mp_agent can create a database with that name, own it and, on PostgreSQL, rename it. purge drops mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_*, mpdata_test_{{e.db_name}}_*, {{e.db_name}}_dev, {{e.db_name}} and test_{{e.db_name}}_* on every running local dialect.
database_urls._drivers: Agent commands write "$PG_URL/<name>" and "$MSSQL_URL/<name>"; data-plane calls write `--target-db local:<name>` and mp-data supplies the data.env server URL. The toolkit maps postgresql:// to SQLAlchemy postgresql+psycopg and mssql:// to mssql+mssqlpython. Django's django-environ reads both as-is (mssql:// gives ENGINE mssql; the overlay sets OPTIONS python_driver mssql_python).

system_packages._why: WeasyPrint 70 (libpangoft2), pyodbc imported by mssql-django (libodbc.so.2), ODBC Driver 18 bundled by mssql-python-odbc (libltdl.so.7). msodbcsql18 is not needed. See environment item syslibs.

app_template._verify: After `git clone --depth 1 --branch 2026.03.09`, `git rev-parse HEAD^{commit}` must print commit. tag_object is what `git ls-remote` shows for refs/tags/2026.03.09; never compare HEAD with it.
app_template._why: Last tag on Django 5.2 (2026.03.10 moves to Django 6.0.3); it targets Python 3.13. Its post-gen hook runs `uv add`, so uv must be on PATH. new-app sets UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER to uv_exclude_newer so the lock and `new-app --check` are reproducible.
app_template._answers: Passed with --no-input; keys are exactly the template's cookiecutter.json keys, and choice values must be one of its choices (cookiecutter 2.7.1 raises ValueError otherwise). cloud_provider becomes "Azure" when e.hosting.provider is azure-app-service, which adds django-storages[azure]==1.14.6. use_whitenoise stays "y": the pre-gen hook exits 1 when use_whitenoise is n and cloud_provider is None. ci_tool None: target CI is written at the repo root by S4.template.

app_packages._removed: The overlay removes psycopg[c] (no wheels, needs libpq-dev), redis, hiredis, django-redis and django-anymail, then runs uv lock.
app_packages._notice: mssql-python pulls mssql-python-odbc 18.6.2.2, which bundles ODBC Driver 18 under a Microsoft licence; NOTICE.md lists it. datacompy and pytest-regressions serve the vendored equivalence harness.

app_assets._rule: Front-end files an area vendors under app/<slug>/<area>/static/<area>/vendor/, downloaded from exactly this URL by the S5 task that needs them (invoicegen dashboard: Chart.js). The task writes the area's THIRD_PARTY.md with version, URL, the sha256 it downloaded and licence; NOTICE.md lists it at S6.

toolkit_packages._rule: uv dependency groups, all declared by S0.workspace. Never extract-msg (GPL), pycel (GPL) or formulas (EUPL).

reference_engine._mirror_why: repo1.maven.org answered 404/429 from a cloud container early on 2026-10-16 and 200 later that day; the Google mirror is tried first and repo1 second, with the same SHA-256 checks.

jars._note: UCanAccess's own Jackcess fork; query formatter at io.github.spannm.jackcess.impl.query.QueryImpl

reference_engine.runtime_jars: resolved: no extra runtime jars (jackcess declares poi as optional; OleUtil falls back by reflection)
reference_engine.jdk: Temurin jdk-21.0.12.1+1 at $HOME/.local/share/modernization/jdk-21 (JAVA_HOME in the env file); see stack.jdk. The jars are Java 11 bytecode.
reference_engine.app_functions: compiled Java classes registered with UcanaccessConnection.addFunctions need @net.ucanaccess.ext.FunctionType annotations. Only Java that other engagements can reuse lives in pipeline:java/; start_jvm (toolkit.reference.bridge) compiles it with javac into a jar under the process TMPDIR at each JVM start, so no task owns vendor/app-functions.jar and vendor/ holds only the fetched jars (the toolkit root is read-only in mp-data's jail and in a pinned release). Prefer correlated-subquery rewrites.

jdk._why: JPype embeds the JVM in-process and finds libjvm through JAVA_HOME, so Java cannot run in Docker; javac compiles app functions. Installed in user space by environment item jdk.

e2e.rule: pin to the version whose browser build is present, else latest that supports the host OS; preflight proves launch
e2e._why: playwright 1.56.0 refuses to install browsers on Ubuntu 26.04; 1.58.0's chromium-1208 is preinstalled here and launches. Never install with --with-deps (no sudo).

guard._rule: copydetect parameters the guard reads; tasks never tune them. disable_filtering keeps comments, string literals and prose in the comparison.

constraints: Never commit client or Microsoft material: source files and exports (.accdt, .accdb, .accde, .mdb, .mde, .laccdb, .ldb, .mdw, .xlsm, .xlsb, .xls, .xlam, .bas, .cls, .frm, .frx, .msg, .bak), rendered samples (.pdf, .eml, .xlsx), anything under {{p.private}}, data values, or verbatim VBA, query or macro text. Paraphrase. Once S0 has built it, run `mp-data guard {{p.records}}/engagement.json --repo {{p.pipeline}} --repo {{p.target_repo}}` before reporting done; it checks every file `git add -A` would add in both repos.

Treat all source data as client data, even in the public demo: never put rows or values in tracked files, prompts, notes or your final answer; use counts, column names and hashes. Anything that runs on the engagement dataset runs through mp-data and is redacted; there is no opt-out. Unredacted diffs are allowed only on goldens/synthetic datasets.

{{p.private}} has two zones. The design zone, which you may read: {{p.private}}/out/ (scrubbed model and inventory; the reference catalog and generated SQL under out/reference/), {{p.private}}/review/ (reviewer scratch) and {{p.private}}/synthetic/ (outputs derived only from committed synthetic seeds: reference DBs, JUnit and matrices, pytest-regressions files, e2e media). The data zone: sources/, datasets/, workbook/, reference/, goldens/, corpus/, results/, logs/, assets/ and scrub-map.json under {{p.private}}. Never open, list, cat, query or copy a data-zone path; only mp-data reads it, and inside mp-run its directories are empty. Write synthetic outputs under {{p.private}}/synthetic/. Commands that touch only the design zone and committed files run as `uv run toolkit ...` with full output: debug there, on synthetic seeds.

A data-plane call is one standalone command, `mp-data [--slot <slot>] [--if-built] <command> {{p.records}}/engagement.json ...`, with no pipe, redirection, &&, ;, substitution, subshell, cd or environment prefix. Never combine mp-data with other shell; run any follow-up check as a separate command. Its stdout is one JSON summary without data values; the full output stays in the data zone. Code that a data-plane call starts (the app under `equivalence --adapter django`, app-function rewrites under reference and golden) runs read-only except the data zone, $TMPDIR and the call's declared outputs, with the mp_runner database login: never make that code write anywhere else.

Engagement rows enter only local databases whose names start with mpdata_ (mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_stage1, mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate, mpdata_test_{{e.db_name}}_<slot>), only through mp-data or the operator, and the login in your PG_URL and MSSQL_URL (mp_agent) is refused there. Your databases are {{e.db_name}}_dev (schema only), {{e.db_name}} (app dev, synthetic data only) and the test databases test_{{e.db_name}}_<slot> named by MP_DB_SUFFIX. Never create a database whose name starts with mpdata_, never drop or reset a database your own commands did not create, and do not run docker, psql or sqlcmd yourself.
Use scrubbed tokens such as <SECRET-1> and <EMAIL-3> as they are; never ask for or reconstruct the original values.

Secrets are referenced, never handled. Secret values live only in $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env or a secret store, named by refs in the engagement's secrets block (`env:NAME`, `pass:<path>`); never in the env file, code, tracked files, prompts or notes. Do not print, echo, request or read secret values, environment dumps (env, printenv, set), data.env or credential files. Code reads secrets from the environment variables or refs the engagement names. If a step needs a secret value, list it in manual_steps.

Pushes to a client target repo go only through `mp-data push {{p.records}}/engagement.json --branch <branch>`, and its pull requests and Actions runs only through `mp-data gh {{p.records}}/engagement.json -- pr <create|view|list|checks|merge> ...` or `-- run <list|view> ...` (gh's output comes back in the summary's messages); both use the token from secrets.github_push.ref without printing it. Never store a token, set a credential helper or run `gh auth` for a client repo. Other pushes use `git push` with the operator's own login.

Run every command in your prompt exactly as written and report each one verbatim with its exit code; a reworded or missing command counts as not run. They come in three forms: `mp-run --eng {{p.records}}/engagement.json --slot <slot> -- '<command>'` (sources the env file, sets MP_DB_SUFFIX, changes to {{p.pipeline}} unless the command starts with cd, and runs it under bubblewrap with the data zone, data.env and Docker hidden and the installed tools, Claude settings and git hooks read-only); `mp-data --slot <slot> <command> ...` (a data-plane call); and, only in an S0 run in bootstrap mode, `. {{p.env_file}} && export MP_DB_SUFFIX=<slot> && cd {{p.pipeline}} && { <command>; }`. Your shell resets between calls: run any other command in the same form as your prompt's commands, with your own slot (inside the mp-run quotes, write a single quote as '\''). Never wrap an mp-data call in mp-run.

Client engagements (bootstrap false) run without the Claude Code sandbox. A PreToolUse hook blocks every Bash call that is not exactly one mp-run or mp-data call; Read, Edit and Write are denied on the data zone, other engagements and data.env; Edit and Write also on the installed tools, the Claude Code settings, the git hooks and git config, and the session settings; Read also on /proc. Demo engagements run their commands through mp-run too from S1 on, so a task that only works by reading the data zone fails in the demo as well.

Tools come from the environment preflight: uv, jq, Python 3.13, the JDK, system libraries, browsers and database containers in user space, and the system's bubblewrap. The orchestrator runs its commands directly, never through mp-run or an agent, because they need Docker and data.env; do not run them yourself. There is no sudo: never pip install into the system Python or run apt-get install. If a tool is missing, report blocked naming the environment item.

Reviewers run only the verify commands of the tasks they review (a task's acceptance commands only when it has no verify list and they are read-only), never edit files, and write any outputs under {{p.private}}/review/<your slot>/: only quiet summaries, regenerated design files and synthetic outputs. That folder is in the design zone, so you may read your own outputs there; never read a data-zone path.
Edit only the paths your task owns and never the paths it lists as never-edit. List anything else you need in requests.
Do not commit or push; the integrate or checkpoint step does that, staging owned paths only. Never run `git add -A` or `git add .`.

Dependencies are declared at S0 (toolkit: stack.toolkit_packages) and S4 (app: stack.app_packages). If you need a package that is not declared, stop with status blocked and requests: ["dependency: <spec> for <reason>"]; the orchestrator adds it on the stage branch and re-runs your task. Never edit pyproject.toml or uv.lock unless your task owns them.

Pipeline tool tests use only generated or hand-written synthetic fixtures, kept under the toolkit/tests/fixtures/<name>/ directory your task owns; never content copied from a client or Microsoft file. The guard still copy-checks fixtures.

Never skip, xfail or delete a test, loosen a tolerance or a guard parameter, or edit a golden file to get green. Goldens change only through `golden record` (mp-data for the engagement dataset), and any change is reported in notes.
App code computes every result from the database. Never read golden files, and never branch on dataset identity, row ids or seed numbers.
Prefer the tools in your task's reuse lists. If one does not fit, report blocked with evidence instead of writing a replacement.
Clean room: do not open or copy code from access2flow (growth-slowly/access2flow_MicrosoftAccess). It has no licence.
Keep the app database-portable: it must pass on PostgreSQL and SQL Server, so no PostgreSQL-only features.
Keep the front half target-neutral: model, rules, goldens, synthetic datasets and the equivalence protocol are JSON, CSV or Markdown and must not depend on Django.
analysis/rules.* are frozen after the S1 gate; only an approved change order (S1.change_order) changes them, and spec-check fails on any other change.
{{p.records}}/answers.md holds the client's answers and overrides assumptions recorded in notes. It states rules, not data: no customer names, amounts or row values.
If only a human or a Windows + Access machine can do a step, finish everything else and list it in manual_steps; report blocked only if your acceptance cannot pass without it.
Record assumptions, and questions for the client, in notes.

In demo engagements whose target repo is on GitHub, integrate and checkpoint run `mp-data guard {{p.records}}/engagement.json --repo {{p.pipeline}} --repo {{p.target_repo}} --history` before every push, so a leak in history is caught before the repo is made public and on every push after.

stages.title: Intake and health check
prepare: jq -e '.bootstrap == true' {{p.records}}/engagement.json >/dev/null || uv run toolkit fetch --jars

gate.name: Health check delivered
client: Read {{p.target}}/docs/health-check.md: one page, object names and counts only, no data values, effort and price band from {{p.private}}/out/estimate.json (pipeline.json pricing_tiers and pricing)

New source: compare the counts in {{p.records}}/inventory.lock.json with what the client said about the app (tables, forms, reports, workbooks), then approve them; later runs compare against this lock
Check that {{p.records}}/source.lock.json lists every file the client sent (the design file, and the one data copy or back end when the client sent it) with bytes and SHA-256

If the health check names a custom quote (more than one data back end, a compiled-only file or a link parse cannot classify), S0 is not ready by design: the parse exit criterion with --fail-on fails. Send the health check with a custom quote and do not offer the fixed-price stages. An encrypted or password-protected file stops parse with 'encrypted source: custom quote' before any health check: ask the prospect for an unencrypted copy, or quote custom

Send the health check to the prospect: when target.mode is local, print {{p.target}}/docs/health-check.md to PDF into a folder outside both repos and outside {{p.private}} and attach it to your email; when the client owns the target repo, send the link to docs/health-check.md on the S0 branch
Offer the paid assessment from pipeline.json pricing_tiers, credited toward the migration

Access kinds, if the client buys Stage 1 alone: take the price from stage1.price_usd.point in {{p.private}}/out/estimate.json, record commercial.quote and commercial.budget_hours (stage1.hours.point) in {{p.records}}/engagement.json, and add stage1 to commercial.purchased

If the prospect buys nothing more (health-check is the last purchased offer): the retention end date is this gate's date plus data_policy.retention_days_after_acceptance. Note it in the S0 row of {{p.records}}/log.md, run `mp-data purge {{p.records}}/engagement.json --dry-run` in a plain terminal now, and run it without --dry-run on that date (pipeline docs/runbook.md section 7)
Record the approval in {{p.records}}/gates.json as S0.approved (YYYY-MM-DD), and your gate and review minutes in the log.md row, before merging
demo: Every count matches expected_inventory: the inventory --expect exit criterion passed in the integrate report, and the S0.parse notes give a reason for every parse warning
Open {{p.target}}/docs/health-check.md: it reads well as a sales artifact (one page, names and counts only, effort and price band from pricing_tiers and pricing)
Skim the S0 diff in both repos: no source file, no VBA, query or macro text, no data values; the guard and the hook probes passed

Check that mp-data, mp-run and mp-bash-hook in $HOME/.local/bin are copies of scripts/: `cd {{p.pipeline}} && cmp scripts/mp-data $HOME/.local/bin/mp-data && cmp scripts/mp-run $HOME/.local/bin/mp-run && cmp scripts/mp-bash-hook $HOME/.local/bin/mp-bash-hook`, and that the hooks environment check passes in both clones (pipeline docs/runbook.md 2(c))
Record the approval in {{p.records}}/gates.json as S0.approved (YYYY-MM-DD), and your gate and review minutes in the log.md row, before merging

tasks.goal: Make the pipeline repo a locked uv project with every toolkit dependency, the engagement loader, the quiet-output helper and the client data plane: mp-data for engagement data, which runs each toolkit child in its own jail, mp-run and the Bash hook that confine every other command of a client session, and the client-session settings generator. Engagement rows stay in mpdata_* databases that the agent role cannot open. Put the engagement's source in the data zone with its size and SHA-256 checked against the pins, or recorded when there are none. Make both repos refuse source files, sample outputs and private data. In delivery mode the tools exist: reuse them, fix only what this engagement needs, and set up the target repo.
