build: uv project. pyproject.toml: name modernization-toolkit, requires-python ">=3.13,<3.14", [project.scripts] toolkit = "toolkit.cli:main". dependencies = stack.toolkit_packages.main; [dependency-groups] excel and dev = the same groups; every pin exact as in the stack. Build backend hatchling (requires ["hatchling>=1.27"]) with [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["toolkit", "harness"]. [tool.uv] exclude-newer = "2026-10-16T00:00:00Z" and default-groups = ["dev", "excel"]. [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts = "--import-mode=importlib", testpaths = ["toolkit/tests", "harness/tests"] and norecursedirs = [".*", "*.egg", "build", "dist", "node_modules", "templates", "vendor"], so pytest never collects templates/ (templates/feature-app/tests/ and templates/e2e/ import Django and the app). [tool.ruff] target-version = "py313" and extend-exclude = ["templates/django-overlay"]. Run `uv lock` and commit uv.lock (about 160 KB with these pins, under the pipeline repo's 1024 KB hook limit). .python-version holds 3.13. Never pip-install into the system Python (PEP 668).

.gitignore: .venv/, __pycache__/, *.pyc, .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, vendor/, engagements/*/paths.local.json, .mp-probe. The records .gitignore holds paths.local.json (the same file serves a client's separate records repo).

toolkit/cli.py: `toolkit <cmd>` discovers subcommands from toolkit/commands/*.py. Module foo_bar is subcommand foo-bar; each module defines add_arguments(parser) and run(args) -> int and may add its own sub-subcommands (dataset export|validate). Parallel tasks therefore never edit a shared file. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 usage or input error. Under MP_QUIET=1, argparse errors and uncaught exceptions also end in one summary line (status error, exit 2) whose message holds the exception type and module:line, never the exception text.

toolkit/engagement.py: load(path) per docs/contracts.md#engagement-loading. It reads engagement.json, the sibling paths.local.json (format_version 1) and the optional source.lock.json and inventory.lock.json; substitutes the six p. placeholders written in double braces (p.pipeline, p.target_repo, p.target, p.private, p.records, p.env_file); fills null pins (source.bytes, sha256, commit, data_copy_sha256, backends[].sha256) from source.lock.json, engagement values winning; loads inventory.lock.json as inventory_lock; derives db_name (engagement db_name, else the id with every character outside [a-z0-9] turned into _, which must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,40}$); ignores keys that start with _ at every depth; exits 2 naming the field when an unresolved double-brace placeholder or a <...> marker is left in a non-underscore value, or when engagement records is set and differs from paths.local.json records. Every command that takes an engagement uses it. toolkit/tests/conftest.py gives later tests three fixtures: make_engagement(tmp_path, **fields) writing engagement.json and paths.local.json, make_git_repo(tmp_path), and quiet (sets MP_QUIET=1).

toolkit/quiet.py per docs/contracts.md#quiet-output: summary(status, command, exit_code, engagement, counts, rates, cells, sha256s, columns, tables, units, mismatches, paths, messages) prints exactly one JSON line on stdout when MP_QUIET=1, written at exit even after an exception, and human text otherwise; status follows the exit code (ok for 0, failed for 1 and 5, error for anything else), with two exit-0 exceptions: a command that wrote a lock instead of comparing (fetch --record-if-unset, inventory --expect) reports recorded, and a command allowed to find nothing (equivalence --allow-empty) reports no-data; progress goes to stderr. Every command uses it. test_quiet.py is parametrized over every module in toolkit/commands/ with test ids equal to the module names (for example test_quiet[parse]); each case runs the command with MP_QUIET=1 and a bad argument and asserts one stdout line that validates against toolkit/schemas/summary.schema.json and exit 2. Later tasks run it with -k <their modules>, so every command is held to the contract.

toolkit/schemas/summary.schema.json per docs/contracts.md#summary-schema (that section wins on key names): required status (ok, recorded, no-data or not-built with exit 0, not-built only from mp-data --if-built; failed for exit 1 or 5; error for anything else), command (the subcommand words, for example 'golden record') and exit_code (integer); optional engagement (id), counts (non-negative integers), rates (numbers from 0 to 1: min_cell, pooled, coverage_adjusted, characterization, empty_share, match), cells (equivalence: list of {dataset, db, status ok or empty, passed, failed, errors, skipped, not_implemented, total, rate}, rate null when empty; results summarize: the results.json cell fields without not_passed, that is {suite, dataset, db, passed, failed, errors, skipped, not_implemented, total, rate}, with no status and rate 0 when total is 0), units (list of {id, status, reason} with optional dataset, db, matched and total: unit ids with statuses and reasons such as ok, needs-params or action-query, or per-unit match counts), tables (list of {table, dialect, dataset_rows, target_rows, digest_match, fk_orphans}: per dialect and table, for example stage1; a field a command cannot fill is null), sha256s (64-hex digests), columns (name to list of column names), mismatches ({unit, dataset, db, columns: {name: count}}), paths (absolute paths inside the pipeline repo, the target repo, the records dir or the design zone), messages (at most 50 strings of at most 200 characters) and log (set by mp-data; absent for not-built and pin); no values anywhere; additionalProperties false at every level; the whole summary is one line.

`toolkit engagement-lint <eng>` with toolkit/schemas/engagement.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12). The schema has a property for every field that engagements/_template/engagement.json and the two demos carry, with additionalProperties false on the top level and on source, target, app, database, data_policy, secrets and scope, and keys starting with _ allowed at every level (patternProperties ^_, any value; the loader ignores them). data_policy.execution is the enum local or cloud-allowed. Demo-only keys are optional properties: source.url, git, branch, commit, clone_dir, vba_export, sample_outputs, on_mismatch, content_md5, etag and last_modified, and scope.email and scope.dashboard. The template and both demos also carry these optional properties: source.licence (S6.handover reads it), source.data_copy_sha256 (64 hex or null), target.local_path, commercial.milestones (array of {offer, when, pct}) and environment.windows_box.copies (array, empty allowed; purge lists it in the destruction record). scope.areas_hint, must_keep and foundation are arrays of strings (empty allowed); source.backends items are {path, sha256, password_ref}, source.external_links items are {name, type} with type odbc-sqlserver, sharepoint, excel or text, and environment.windows_box.copies items are {path, what}, both required strings (all three with additionalProperties false); target.repo is null or a GitHub owner/name matching ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (mp-data push and gh require origin https://github.com/<target.repo>); database.stage1, secrets.github_push and secrets.entra are objects or null (the demos carry null); every secret ref (secrets.github_push.ref, accdb_password_ref, stage1_target_url_ref, staging_db_url_ref, entra.client_secret_ref and source.backends[].password_ref) is null or matches ^(env:[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*|pass:\S+)$. Lint adds the driver's checks: source.kind in pipeline.json source_kinds; id ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and at most 40 characters; app.slug ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,29}$ and not in pipeline.json slug_reserved; the derived db_name; no <...> template marker in a non-underscore string; source.compiled_only not true; when records is set it equals paths.local.json records and, for bootstrap false, lies outside paths.pipeline. It prints every problem and exits 1. test_engagement.py: both demo engagements pass; an unedited copy of engagements/_template fails naming at least id, source.kind and app.slug; an unknown key fails and an unknown key starting with _ passes; data_policy.execution outside the enum fails; a secret ref of another form (also in source.backends[].password_ref) an external_links type outside the enum, and a windows_box.copies item without what or with another key fail; a records value that differs from paths.local.json fails; a missing paths.local.json exits 2.

`toolkit fetch` (toolkit/fetch.py, toolkit/commands/fetch.py) per docs/contracts.md#source-lock. `fetch <eng> --verify [--record-if-unset]`. URL source (northwind): when source.path is missing, send a HEAD request first and compare last_modified, etag and content_md5 (hex in the engagement, base64 in the Content-MD5 header) when pinned; any difference exits 1 before downloading (drift: report blocked, never update a pin); then download to source.path and check bytes and SHA-256. A file that is present is only hashed, with no network. Git source (invoicegen): `git clone --branch <branch> <git> <clone_dir>` when missing, `git -C <clone_dir> checkout --detach <commit>`, check `git rev-parse HEAD`, then the bytes and SHA-256 of source.path. Local source (clients): the operator has copied the files into the private sources/ folder; hash source.path, source.data_copy (the one data back end) and every source.backends[].path. Compare with the engagement pins when set (source.bytes, sha256, commit, data_copy_sha256, backends[].sha256), else with the records source.lock.json. With --record-if-unset and neither present, write source.lock.json per docs/contracts.md#source-lock (format_version 1, recorded date, source {path relative to the private dir, bytes, sha256, git {url, branch, commit} or null}, data_copy {path, bytes, sha256} or null, and backends with path, bytes and sha256; the loader fills source.data_copy_sha256 from data_copy.sha256) and exit 0 with status recorded and the message 'recorded; approve at the S0 gate'. No pin, no lock and no --record-if-unset exits 2. Any mismatch exits 1 and never rewrites a pin (source.on_mismatch). For every source kind, xlsm included, it also ensures the vendor jars in the toolkit root's vendor/ (toolkit/tests/test_reference.py starts a JVM in every `uv run pytest -q toolkit` from the northwind S2 on, invoicegen's stages too). That is the toolkit root mp-data runs: for demos (bootstrap true) the pipeline worktree, so every prepare list's fetch line restores them there; for clients the pinned release, whose vendor/ `mp-data pin` fills, so the S0 (clients only, so a demo's S0 bootstrap never needs it before fetch exists), S1 and S2 prepare lists also run `uv run toolkit fetch --jars` for the pipeline worktree's own vendor/ (gitignored, so later stages keep it). `fetch --jars`: download stack.reference_engine.jars into vendor/ from stack.reference_engine.maven_mirror first and repo1.maven.org second, check each SHA-256, skip files that already match. Summaries hold sizes, hashes and status only. test_fetch.py serves fixture bytes and HEAD headers from a local http.server (including a drifted etag that must exit 1 without a download) and a local bare git repo; it never downloads the real sources.

toolkit/secrets.py (decisions L3.5, L12.2): resolve(ref, field) for the two ref forms of engagement secrets. Outside mp-data's jail (in toolkit/dataplane.py and for the operator), env:NAME reads variable NAME from $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env (parsed as `export NAME=value` lines with literal values; never from the process environment and never from the env file) and pass:<path> runs `pass show <path>` and takes the first line. Inside the jail (MP_SANDBOX=mp-data), where data.env and the pass store are hidden, it reads only the variable MP_SECRET_<FIELD> that dataplane.py set for that field (FIELD: the field path upper-cased, each run of characters outside [A-Z0-9] replaced by _, for example MP_SECRET_SECRETS_GITHUB_PUSH_REF or MP_SECRET_SOURCE_BACKENDS_0_PASSWORD_REF). A missing file, an unset name, a failing pass, a missing MP_SECRET_ variable or any other scheme exits 2 naming the field, never the value. Values go only to the caller in memory: never to stdout, stderr, logs, argv or files, and no command prints one. Callers: toolkit push and gh, stage1 --target-db secret:<ref> (S3.move), and the readers of an encrypted source or back end (secrets.accdb_password_ref, source.backends[].password_ref). test_secrets.py: env: from a fixture data.env under a temporary HOME; pass: through a stub `pass` on PATH; under MP_SANDBOX=mp-data the value comes from MP_SECRET_<FIELD> and data.env is never opened; an unknown scheme exits 2; no value appears in captured output.

scripts/mp-data (bash; installed as $HOME/.local/bin/mp-data; decisions L1, L12.4). Form: `mp-data [--slot <slot>] [--if-built] <command> <args>`, global flags before the command. <command> is one of fetch, parse, dataset, guard, reference, golden, stage1, equivalence, purge, results, push, gh, or pin; anything else exits 2 and runs nothing. --slot must match ^[a-z0-9_]{1,24}$ (default orchestrator). The engagement is the first argument ending in /engagement.json (exit 2 when there is none; pin takes none); mp-data reads it and the sibling paths.local.json with jq. It sources $HOME/.config/modernization/env (never data.env: toolkit/dataplane.py reads that file itself and exports none of it), exports MP_DB_SUFFIX=<slot>, changes to the toolkit root itself and runs `uv run --project <root> python -m toolkit.dataplane <command> <args>`, every argument passed through unchanged (for example equivalence --only-areas). The toolkit root is paths.pipeline when the engagement has bootstrap true. Otherwise it is the reviewed release $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit@<sha> named in $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit.pin, run with UV_CACHE_DIR=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-cache and that worktree's own .venv (both synced by mp-data pin, read-only inside mp-run and denied to the Edit and Write tools, so agent commands cannot alter the code that reads client data); with nothing pinned it exits 2 with 'no reviewed toolkit: run mp-data pin <sha>'. So every call is one standalone command with no shell set-up around it, which is the only shape the client-session Bash hook allows. --if-built: when the engagement has bootstrap true and <root>/toolkit/commands/<command>.py does not exist, print {"status":"not-built","command":"<command>","exit_code":0,...} and exit 0 without running anything; with bootstrap false it changes nothing (a missing module exits 2).

mp-data child environment and database guard (decisions L3.4, L12.3): toolkit/dataplane.py reads $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env when present (the `export NAME=value` lines, parsed, never sourced) and gives the toolkit child mp-data's environment plus MP_QUIET=1, MP_DB_SUFFIX, MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX=mpdata_test_, MP_SANDBOX=mp-data, TMPDIR (next item) and the database URLs of its command, each under two names. equivalence, reference build, run and selfcheck, and golden record run agent-written code (the Django app, app-function rewrites), so they get the runner URLs: MP_RUNNER_PG_URL as MP_DATA_PG_URL and PG_URL, MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL as MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL and MSSQL_URL. stage1 and purge run only toolkit code and get the superuser URLs MP_DATA_PG_URL and MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL under the same two names. Every other command gets no database URL. A URL that data.env lacks leaves both its names unset, so the mp_agent URLs of the env file never reach a data-plane command, and no other data.env value reaches the child (secrets: next item). For purge it also sets MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES: the db_names of every other engagement, comma-separated (empty when there is none), read before the jail starts from each engagement.json under $HOME/engagements/*/record/ and {{p.pipeline}}/engagements/ except this engagement and _template (db_name, or the id with every character outside [a-z0-9] replaced by _). The jail hides those directories, and purge needs the names to keep a database of another engagement whose db_name extends this one. Before stage1, equivalence, reference build, run or selfcheck, or golden record runs, dataplane connects with the superuser URL of each dialect whose URL it hands over and exits 2, running nothing, when a database named mpdata_* there is owned by a role other than postgres or mp_runner (SQL Server: sa or mp_runner); a server that does not answer is left to the command. Reason: mp_agent has CREATEDB (CREATE ANY DATABASE), so it could create an mpdata_ database, own it and read the rows later (as dbo on SQL Server, or on PostgreSQL by renaming the database past the pg_hba reject line). mp-data refuses (exit 2, runs nothing) a --target-db that is a literal URL or a local:<name> whose name does not start with mpdata_, so engagement rows only ever enter mpdata_* databases (Stage 1 mpdata_<db_name>_stage1; Django test databases of data-plane equivalence runs mpdata_test_<db_name>_<slot>). It creates the parent directory of any --out, --report or --matrix path and the --junit-dir directory before it runs the command, so pipeline.json needs no mkdir. Those paths, with symlinks resolved, must lie inside paths.pipeline, paths.target_repo, paths.records or paths.private, and the two outputs that hold engagement values, `dataset export --out` and `guard --report`, must lie in the data zone; anything else exits 2 and runs nothing, so no data-plane call copies rows to a path an agent can read.

mp-data's jail (decisions L12.2): toolkit/dataplane.py runs the child as `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --die-with-parent --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc`, then the writable binds, then the masks, then `-- <root>/.venv/bin/toolkit <command> <args>` (no uv inside the jail: Django cells run {{p.target}}/app/.venv/bin/python and exit 2 naming `cd {{p.target}}/app && uv sync --locked` when it is missing, S2.harness, decisions L13.7). Writable (`--bind`, each created first when missing): this engagement's data-zone directories (sources, datasets, workbook, reference, goldens, corpus, results, logs and assets under paths.private) and its scrub-map.json, which parse writes; a fresh TMPDIR that dataplane creates for the call inside the data zone (tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='tmp-', dir=<paths.private>/logs), so already writable) and removes afterwards (a TMPDIR that purge already deleted is no error): temporary files of a data-plane call can hold engagement values (Django test files, pytest-regressions output), and a directory under /tmp would be readable by every agent of the same user, through mp-run and through the Read tool; the --junit-dir directory and the parent directory of each --out, --report and --matrix path; and per command: fetch the records dir (source.lock.json) and the toolkit root's vendor/ (jars); guard the pre-commit cache $HOME/.local/share/modernization/pre-commit, which it uses as PRE_COMMIT_HOME (agents cannot write there); golden record {{p.target}}/goldens/; push and gh the target repo's git directories (`git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` and `--git-common-dir`); purge paths.private itself and the records dir (decisions L13.6: purge empties paths.private; directories that are mount points in the jail, paths.private included, stay, empty). Everything else is read-only, including the design zone, both repos and $HOME; so `reference build` writes only the engagement database through mp-data, and the seed databases in {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/ are built with `uv run toolkit reference build <eng> --dataset seeds|seed-N` (contracts §9; `--dataset all` exits 2). The masks: --tmpfs over every other engagement's private/ and record/ under $HOME/engagements, for every command, purge included (purge gets their db_names in MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES instead, decisions L13.6), over the pass store (${PASSWORD_STORE_DIR:-$HOME/.password-store}; bwrap cannot bind /dev/null over a directory, tested with bubblewrap 0.11.1), and over the directories that hold unix sockets of the operator's own processes: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (default /run/user/<uid>: the session bus, the systemd user manager, rootless Docker and containerd, ssh and gpg agents), ${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-<uid> and /run/screen/S-<user> (each when present). A read-only mount does not stop connect() on a unix socket: under --ro-bind / / without that tmpfs, the child read the systemd user manager's properties over the session bus (tested here with bubblewrap 0.11.1), and that manager can start a command outside any jail; with the tmpfs the bus and Docker were unreachable. Then --ro-bind /dev/null over $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env, /var/run/docker.sock and the unix socket DOCKER_HOST names when it lies outside $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (each when present). --dev /dev gives the child its own /dev/shm, so no tmpfs shared with agents is writable (/tmp and /var/tmp are read-only under --ro-bind / /). The host network is kept, so the 127.0.0.1 databases work. Secrets: before it starts the child, dataplane resolves with toolkit.secrets exactly the refs the command needs (push and gh: secrets.github_push.ref; stage1 --target-db secret:<name>: secrets.<name>, for example MP_SECRET_SECRETS_STAGE1_TARGET_URL_REF for secret:stage1_target_url_ref; fetch, parse, dataset, guard, reference and golden: secrets.accdb_password_ref and source.backends[].password_ref when set) and passes each value only as MP_SECRET_<FIELD> in the child's environment. So code that a data-plane call runs (the Django app under `equivalence --adapter django`, app-function rewrites under reference and golden) can read this engagement's data but can write only into the data zone, TMPDIR and the call's declared outputs, and never sees data.env, the pass store, Docker, the operator's session sockets or another engagement.

toolkit/dataplane.py (docs/contracts.md#quiet-output) runs `toolkit <command> <args>` as a child in that jail with that environment, writes the child's full stdout and stderr to <paths.private>/logs/<utc-ts>-<slot>-<pid>-<command>.log (UTC timestamp YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ, the slot, this process id and the subcommand; chmod 600, created exclusively, so parallel agents never share a log), validates the summary line against toolkit/schemas/summary.schema.json, adds log (the log path) and prints exactly that one line. When <paths.private>/corpus/strings.txt exists, a summary line that contains any of its strings is withheld. When the summary is missing, invalid or withheld, it prints its own summary with status error and no toolkit text, and exits 2 if the subcommand had exited 0. Otherwise the exit code is the subcommand's. dataplane.run(argv, runner=...) takes an injectable runner for tests.

`mp-data push <eng> --branch <branch>` (toolkit/commands/push.py; decisions L3.5): pushes local branch <branch> of a client target repo to origin <branch> (the runbook uses it for stage branches, gate commits, dependency adds, change-order merges and main). It exits 2 when target.mode is not github or secrets.github_push.ref is unset; otherwise it resolves the ref with toolkit.secrets and runs, in paths.target_repo, `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper=<one-shot helper> push origin refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>` with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, so only the repo's own config applies. The one-shot helper answers only for protocol https and host github.com, with username x-access-token and the token (MP_SECRET_SECRETS_GITHUB_PUSH_REF in the jail, read through toolkit.secrets) from that git process's environment, so the token never reaches argv, stdout, stderr, the log or a file. It refuses (exit 2) a branch outside ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$, any force flag, an origin url or pushurl other than https://github.com/<target.repo> (with or without .git), and a target repo whose own git config sets url.*.insteadOf, url.*.pushInsteadOf, remote.origin.proxy or any http.* proxy or ssl key. Repo credential.* keys are allowed: the empty -c credential.helper resets every helper the config names, and the runbook sets an empty helper and useHttpPath there itself. The summary names the branch and the pushed commit in messages. Pipeline and records repos are pushed with the operator's own git credentials, not through mp-data.

`mp-data gh <eng> -- <pr|run> <action> [args]` (toolkit/commands/gh.py; decisions L3.5): allows pr create, view, list, checks and merge, and run list and view (decisions L12.5); refuses -R/--repo, any other subcommand and an origin URL other than the engagement's target repo (exit 2). It runs gh in paths.target_repo with GH_REPO=<target.repo>, GH_CONFIG_DIR set to a new empty directory under TMPDIR (so no gh config file applies) and GH_TOKEN from secrets.github_push.ref, all in that child's environment only. A file argument (--body-file, -F, --template) that resolves into the data zone, data.env or another engagement's directory exits 2, because gh would upload the file. It puts gh's stdout lines (at most 50, each cut to 200 characters) into the summary messages; stderr goes to the log.

`mp-data pin <sha>` (operator only, in a terminal): refuses without a terminal on stdin and stdout (agents' Bash calls have none) and works in the git checkout of the current directory (a pipeline clone or worktree; exit 2 when the current directory is not a git checkout): it refuses a sha that is not an ancestor of origin/main after `git fetch origin` there. Then `git worktree add --detach $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit@<sha> <sha>`, and there, with UV_CACHE_DIR=$HOME/.local/share/modernization/uv-cache (decisions L12.4), `uv sync --locked --all-groups` and `uv run toolkit fetch --jars`; it runs that release's scripts/install-mp-data.sh, so the installed mp-data, mp-run and mp-bash-hook come from the reviewed release; and it writes the sha to $HOME/.local/share/modernization/toolkit.pin. `mp-data pin --status` prints the pinned sha in a summary and exits 1 when nothing is pinned. scripts/install-mp-data.sh copies mp-data, mp-run and mp-bash-hook from its own directory to $HOME/.local/bin (copies with mode 755, never symlinks, so edits in a worktree never change the installed tools) and creates $HOME/.local/share/modernization/; it is idempotent.

test_dataplane.py: an unknown command exits 2; a global flag after the command is refused; a bad --slot exits 2 and a good one reaches the child as MP_DB_SUFFIX; --if-built prints not-built and exits 0 for a bootstrap engagement whose module is missing, and exits 2 for a delivery engagement; a bootstrap engagement runs from paths.pipeline; a delivery engagement with no pin exits 2; equivalence, reference build, run and selfcheck, and golden record children get the MP_RUNNER_ URLs and stage1 and purge the MP_DATA_ URLs from a fixture data.env, each under its own MP_DATA_ name and as PG_URL or MSSQL_URL, other commands get none, a URL missing from data.env leaves both names unset, and no other data.env value reaches the child; purge gets MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES with the db_names of the other fixture engagements (empty when there are none) and no other command gets it; the child's TMPDIR lies under <private>/logs/ and is gone after the call; an existing mpdata_ database owned by mp_agent (fake connection) makes stage1 and equivalence exit 2 before the child runs, while owners postgres, sa and mp_runner pass; the jail argv for each command lists the read-only root, the writable binds of the jail item and then the masks, in that order (a pure function, no bwrap needed), and purge's argv binds paths.private and the records dir writable while another engagement's private/ and record/ stay masked; a real jail run (needs bubblewrap; skipped when MP_SANDBOX is set, because a bwrap inside mp-run is refused) shows data.env, the pass store and another engagement's private/ unreadable, a unix socket listener the test starts in a temporary XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unreachable, a design-zone file and the pipeline read-only, a data-zone directory, TMPDIR and the --out parent writable, and a 127.0.0.1 listener reachable; push gets the token only as MP_SECRET_SECRETS_GITHUB_PUSH_REF and equivalence gets no MP_SECRET_ variable; stage1 with a literal --target-db URL or a local: name without mpdata_ exits 2 and runs nothing; equivalence children get MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX=mpdata_test_; two runs in the same second with different slots or pids write different log files; the parent directory of --out is created; an --out outside the four paths, and a `dataset export --out` outside the data zone, exit 2 and run nothing; push and gh never put the token in argv, stdout or the log, and push runs with hooks disabled; gh refuses -R, subcommands other than pr and run, and a --body-file in the data zone; push refuses an origin pushurl that differs from the target repo; pin refuses without a terminal; a summary that contains a corpus string is withheld and replaced by an error summary. CANARY test: a synthetic engagement under tmp_path whose dataset cells are CANARY-<n> and whose corpus strings.txt lists them, plus an injected runner for parse that prints those cells to stdout and stderr and exits 1. Assert exit code 1, exactly one valid summary line, no 'CANARY-' in anything mp-data printed, and the cells present in the log file.

scripts/mp-run (bash; decisions L3.1, L12.1; installed beside mp-data). Form: `mp-run --eng <records>/engagement.json --slot <slot> -- '<command>'` with exactly one command string and a slot matching ^[a-z0-9_]{1,24}$ (anything else exits 2). It reads <records>/paths.local.json, sources $HOME/.config/modernization/env, exports MP_DB_SUFFIX=<slot> and MP_SANDBOX=mp-run, unsets DOCKER_HOST, and runs `bash -c '<command>'` in paths.pipeline (a command that starts with `cd ` moves itself) under `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --die-with-parent --dev-bind / / --proc /proc` plus, in this order. First the read-only binds (`--ro-bind`, each when present): $HOME/.local/bin, $HOME/.local/share/modernization, $HOME/.local/share/uv, $HOME/.config/modernization, $HOME/.claude, $HOME/.claude.json, $HOME/engagements/<id>/client-session.json, the pipeline worktree's .claude/ and .mcp.json, and the hooks/ directory and config file of the git common directory (`git -C <repo> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`) of the pipeline and target repos. Then the masks: --tmpfs over every data-zone directory of this engagement (sources, datasets, workbook, reference, goldens, corpus, results, logs and assets under paths.private, created first when missing), over every other engagement's private/ and record/ under $HOME/engagements, over the pass store (${PASSWORD_STORE_DIR:-$HOME/.password-store}, a directory: bwrap cannot bind /dev/null over a directory, tested with bubblewrap 0.11.1), and over $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (default /run/user/<uid>), ${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-<uid> and /run/screen/S-<user> (each when present: as in mp-data's jail, the session bus there reaches the systemd user manager, which starts commands outside mp-run, and rootless Docker and containerd keep their sockets there); and --ro-bind /dev/null over <private>/scrub-map.json, $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env, /var/run/docker.sock and the unix socket DOCKER_HOST named when it lies outside $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (each when present). bwrap applies mounts in argument order and a later bind wins: a read-only bind of $HOME/.config/modernization placed after the /dev/null bind over data.env makes data.env readable again (tested on this host), so the masks always come last. So no command in mp-run can change what runs outside it: Claude Code settings, hooks and MCP servers, git hooks and git config (core.fsmonitor, filters), the installed tools, the uv-managed Python and the pinned release; and none can reach a process that runs commands outside it (the systemd user manager, a tmux or screen server, Docker). Credential stores reached through $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (a D-Bus keyring, ssh-agent, gpg-agent) do not work inside mp-run, so git and gh there use gh's file-stored token (`gh auth status` names hosts.yml). A bound .git/config cannot be rewritten (git's lock-and-rename fails even on a writable bind), so `git push -u` inside mp-run prints 'could not write config file' and still exits 0, and `git config` or `git remote` writes fail. The design zone (out/, review/, synthetic/) stays readable and writable; the host network is kept, so 127.0.0.1 databases work; writes into a hidden directory are discarded. The exit code is the command's. test_mp_run.py (needs bubblewrap, environment item bwrap) builds a fixture engagement in a temporary HOME and proves: a data-zone file reads empty, another engagement's private/ is empty, data.env is unreadable although $HOME/.config/modernization is bound read-only before its mask (the order case), writes to $HOME/.local/bin, the pipeline's .claude/ and its git hooks directory fail, `docker info` fails, a unix socket listener the test starts in a temporary XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unreachable, a 127.0.0.1 listener started by the test is reachable, $MP_DB_SUFFIX is set, the working directory is the pipeline, and exit codes 0, 1 and 7 pass through. It runs where mp-run is not already around it (S0 bootstrap acceptance, pipeline CI, the runbook's first-session probe): when MP_SANDBOX is mp-run it skips with that reason, because Ubuntu's AppArmor profile for bwrap refuses a user namespace inside bwrap (on this host a single bwrap runs and a nested one fails), and from S1 on every pytest run is inside mp-run.

scripts/mp-bash-hook (python3 -I, stdlib only, shebang #!/usr/bin/python3 -I; decisions L3.3; installed beside mp-data). Claude Code runs it as the PreToolUse hook for Bash in client sessions; it reads the hook JSON on stdin and takes tool_input.command. It allows the call (exit 0, no output) only when the command is one simple command whose first word is exactly mp-run or mp-data: no newline or carriage return; no $ or backtick outside single quotes and no unbalanced quote (shlex drops quoting, so the hook scans the raw text for these first); split with shlex.shlex(command, posix=True, punctuation_chars=True) and whitespace_split, no token made only of the characters ( ) ; < > | & (operators, redirections, subshells, background); no leading NAME=value assignment; mp-run exactly as `mp-run --eng <path> --slot <slot> -- <one command string>`; mp-data with any arguments except pin (only `mp-data pin --status`). Anything else, or input it cannot parse, exits 2 with this on stderr: client session: run shell commands as mp-run --eng <eng> --slot <slot> -- '<command>', or a data-plane call mp-data ... test_mp_bash_hook.py feeds hook JSON on stdin. Allowed: an mp-run call whose quoted command holds pipes, &&, $HOME and '\'' quotes, and mp-data calls with global flags and a quoted -k '[orders::'. Blocked: ls, a pipe, &&, ;, a trailing &, $(...) and backticks (also inside double quotes), redirections including 2>&1, a FOO=1 prefix, a newline, a subshell, an absolute path to mp-data, mp-run with an extra argument, an unbalanced quote and mp-data pin <sha>.

scripts/client-settings.sh <id> (bash, jq and git; decisions L3.3). <id> is its only argument and it needs no other file from the pipeline checkout, so `git show origin/main:scripts/client-settings.sh | bash -s -- <id>` works. It prints the client-session settings JSON on stdout; the runbook writes it to $HOME/engagements/<id>/client-session.json with chmod 600 and starts the session with `claude --settings` and that file. Every path is absolute and expanded from $HOME, written in Claude Code's absolute form (// plus the path without its leading slash, for example Read(//home/me/engagements/c2026001/private/sources/**)); no ~ and no wildcard inside a path segment; directories end in /**, files do not. Content: disableAllHooks false (so no lower settings scope can switch the hook off); sandbox {enabled: false}; permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode "disable"; permissions.allow ["Bash(mp-run:*)", "Bash(mp-data:*)"], so workflow agents' many distinct mp-run and mp-data calls do not each wait for approval (the PreToolUse Bash hook still runs first and refuses every other shape); permissions.deny holds Read, Edit and Write of every data-zone directory of this engagement (sources, datasets, workbook, reference, goldens, corpus, results, logs, assets under $HOME/engagements/<id>/private) and of its scrub-map.json; Read, Edit and Write of private/ and record/ of every other engagement directory present under $HOME/engagements; Read, Edit and Write of $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env; Edit and Write of $HOME/.local/bin/**, $HOME/.local/share/modernization/**, $HOME/.config/modernization/**, $HOME/.claude/**, $HOME/.claude.json and $HOME/engagements/<id>/client-session.json, and, when $HOME/engagements/<id>/record/paths.local.json exists, of the pipeline worktree's .claude/** and .mcp.json and of hooks/** and config in the git common directory of the pipeline and target repos (the files mp-run binds read-only: the Edit and Write tools act outside mp-run, and these files configure code that runs outside any jail); Read of /proc/** (written Read(//proc/**): the Read tool runs outside any jail, /proc/<pid>/environ of a data-plane child holds its MP_SECRET_ values, and /proc/<pid>/root reaches every denied path under another name); and Monitor; hooks.PreToolUse is [{matcher Bash, hooks [{type command, command $HOME/.local/bin/mp-bash-hook}]}]. Top-level keys are exactly disableAllHooks, hooks, permissions and sandbox. The design zone (out/, review/, synthetic/) and this engagement's record/ are not denied. An id that does not match the engagement id pattern, or a missing $HOME/engagements/<id>, exits 2. test_client_settings.py runs it under a temporary HOME with two engagements and checks the same facts as the acceptance jq line, including the two allow entries.

scripts/dev_db.sh (bash; decisions L3.4, L12.5): the operator's helper for agent databases, in a plain terminal and in S0's tests. It needs Docker, so it never runs inside mp-run, and it provisions nothing: the postgres and mssql environment items create the containers, roles, passwords and pg_hba lines. It sources the env file $HOME/.config/modernization/env itself, never reads data.env and never prints a password. `createdb <name>` and `dropdb <name>` (name ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$ and not starting with mpdata_, else exit 2 before any docker call) act on each dialect whose URL the env file sets and whose container runs, as the agent role inside the container: PostgreSQL `docker exec -e PGPASSWORD mp-pg16 createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -U mp_agent <name>` (dropdb with --if-exists), with PGPASSWORD set from PG_URL for that docker call only, so mp_agent owns the database; SQL Server `docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U mp_agent -b -Q "create database [<name>]"` (drop: `drop database if exists [<name>]`), with SQLCMDPASSWORD from MSSQL_URL, so the mp_agent login is its owner. createdb leaves an existing database unchanged and dropdb ignores a missing one. The S4 and S5 gates use them for the app dev database (the engagement's db_name), which the app then migrates as mp_agent. `url pg|mssql` prints PG_URL or MSSQL_URL (the agent URLs) and exits 1 when it is unset. Any other subcommand (`up` and `check` included) exits 2. test_dev_db.py runs it with a temporary HOME, a fixture env file and a stub `docker` on PATH that records its arguments and environment: the exact docker calls for both dialects, the password only in the docker call's environment (never in argv or output), mpdata_ and malformed names exiting 2 without a docker call, `url pg` printing the fixture PG_URL, and `up` exiting 2.

Pre-commit configs (decisions E1), the same hooks in the pipeline repo and at the target repo root. repo local: hook forbid-source-files (language: fail, files '(?i)([.](accdt|accdb|accde|mdb|mde|laccdb|ldb|mdw|xlsm|xlsb|xls|xlam|bas|cls|frm|frx|msg|bak)$|^(private|data|vendor)/)') and hook forbid-sample-outputs (language: fail, files '(?i)[.](pdf|eml|xlsx)$'); in the pipeline repo only, both have exclude '^toolkit/tests/fixtures/' (fixtures are still copy-checked by the guard). https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks rev v6.0.0: check-added-large-files with args ['--enforce-all', '--maxkb=1024'] in the pipeline repo (pipeline.json is above 500 KB) and ['--enforce-all', '--maxkb=500'] in the target repo. https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit rev v0.17.1: ruff-check with no files filter (S4 relies on it to lint app/). The target-repo config holds only these self-contained hooks (no repo: local hook that calls the toolkit). Install the git hook in both clones: `uv run pre-commit install` in the pipeline repo and `uv run --project <pipeline> pre-commit install` in the target repo (bootstrap mode; in delivery mode mp-run keeps .git/hooks read-only, and the `hooks` environment item installs them before the next stage).

Pipeline CI .github/workflows/ci.yml (on push and pull_request; permissions contents: read; runs-on ubuntu-24.04): actions/checkout@v4; actions/setup-python@v5 with 3.13; actions/setup-node@v4 with 22; actions/setup-java@v4 with distribution temurin and java-version 21 (toolkit tests start a JVM from the northwind S2 on); `sudo apt-get update` and `sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap` and, when `sysctl -n kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` prints 1, `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` (the runner is disposable; test_mp_run.py needs unprivileged user namespaces); `pip install uv==0.13.1`; `uv sync --locked --all-groups`; `uv run toolkit fetch --jars`; `uv run ruff check .`; `uv run pytest -q`; `uv run toolkit guard --hooks-only --repo .`; `node tests/driver/run-stage.test.mjs`. No secrets and no engagement data: the copy guard needs the private corpus and runs locally.

saveastext.py: line-oriented parser for Access SaveAsText: nested Begin/End blocks, quoted strings with doubled-quote escapes, hex continuation lines (0x...), property types dbText, dbMemo, dbBinary, dbLong, dbInteger, dbBoolean and dbByte, and CodeBehindForm/CodeBehindReport sections. Used for forms, reports, queries and macros. Form and report designs also give the layout facts the S6 wireframes need: sections (name and height), controls with type, name, caption, left, top, width and height in twips, the source object of each subform, and tab controls with their pages and the controls on each page. Macros: standalone macro SaveAsText blocks (and the .accdt macros/ parts) are parsed into actions, and the embedded macro blocks of form and report event properties (controls whose event is '[Embedded Macro]') too; both go to objects.json macros[] entries {name, kind: standalone|embedded, owner: null | "form:<form>.<event>" | "report:<report>.<event>", actions: [{action, args: {<argument name>: <object name or scrubbed literal>}}]} (docs/contracts.md#object-model), and controls[].events mark embedded macros. Add a hand-written fixture with one standalone and one embedded macro under toolkit/tests/fixtures/parse/ and a test in test_parse_saveastext.py.

schema.py: table XSDs (od:jetType, od:sqlSType, sizes, required, autonumber, indexes, primary keys) plus relationships into schema.json with the neutral column types text, memo, byte, integer, longinteger, autonumber, single, double, currency, decimal, datetime, yesno, hyperlink, oleobject, complex and guid.

vba.py: split standard modules, class modules and code-behind sections; thin procedure scanner (Sub, Function, Property Get/Let/Set with Public, Private, Friend and Static; line continuations ' _'); per-module non-blank line counts excluding lines that start with 'Attribute ' (comment lines count); references to tables, queries and forms, DoCmd calls and DAO use. Accept CRLF and LF (Northwind modules are CRLF; the InvoiceGenerator export and olevba output are LF).
datamacros.py: dataMacros/*.axl into {table, event, actions}; properties/*.axl only into object metadata.

model.py: write schema.json, objects.json, procedures.json and datamacros.json (UTF-8, LF, keys sorted, lists sorted by name) and code/<file-safe module name>.txt with each module's scrubbed VBA (UTF-8, LF; procedures.json names it in code_file; code-behind modules are named Form_<form> and Report_<report>) after validating each against toolkit/schemas/model.schema.json (one $defs entry per file). objects.json also carries facts the counts and the health check need that are not data: query storage (design grid or SQL text), objects with code behind, has_cached_value per formula cell (xlsm), the file count per declared sample_outputs folder (counts only, never file names), form and report layouts, and every linked table with its back-end kind (access, odbc, sharepoint, excel or text) and a back-end number (the connect string itself is scrubbed). Object names follow docs/contracts.md#inventory: tables by name, calculated columns <Table>[<Column>], formula blocks and data validations <Sheet>!<A1 range>, charts <Sheet>!<chart name>.

sources/xlsm.py (finding xlsm-schema-and-coverage-undefined). schema.json: one table per ListObject (name, sheet, ref and header names in order) with neutral column types inferred from cached values; calculated columns get computed: true and their calculatedColumnFormula as written; list validations give choices_from; tables with no business data get role: documentation (InvoiceGenerator: VBAGlossary); keys are inferred (a unique non-blank column) and FKs inferred (all values present in another table's key), both flagged inferred: true for S1 to confirm. objects.json: userforms (name, caption, control names, types and captions from olevba extract_form_strings_extended; the .frx layout is not parsed); sheets with a role (input, template, calculation, dashboard, documentation); formula blocks (contiguous formula ranges outside tables, with the address of every cell and its formula as written, including structured references); defined names (broken #REF! names are warnings, not errors); charts (type and series refs); form-control buttons and shape macro assignments (xl/ctrlProps, drawing macro= attributes, VML x:FmlaMacro); ActiveX controls (xl/activeX, CLSID, handler names); cell comment counts per sheet; VBA library references (REFERENCENAME records). procedures.json: components typed from the PROJECT stream (Module= standard, Class= class, Document= document, BaseClass= userform). When source.vba_export is set, cross-check the line and procedure counts of the exported files with the workbook's modules and report differences as warnings. Cached values and comment texts go to the private workbook/ folder, never into the model. Layout facts for S6.visuals_xlsm, read from the workbook design only: per sheet the column widths, row heights and merged ranges; label cells (constant text cells outside ListObjects on sheets with role input, template or dashboard that no formula and no VBA Range or Cells literal reads or writes; at most 80 characters; scrubbed; any other constant cell is recorded by position only, with value null); ListObject ranges and header names; chart anchors, titles and types; form-control buttons with caption and assigned macro name; and userform controls with type, name, caption and position from the exported .frm text when source.vba_export is set (else names, types and captions from olevba). S2.reference_xlsm rebuilds the seed workbooks from these facts alone (sheets, each ListObject's ref, headers and calculated-column formulas, formula blocks with cell addresses, defined names and scrubbed label cells); constant values never enter the model, and S2 turns input cells into parameters set at run time.

sources/vcs_export.py: msaccess-vcs-addin export folder (forms/, reports/, modules/ *.bas and *.cls, queries/ *.bas and *.sql, tbldefs/, macros/) through the same SaveAsText parser. Table data files in the export are data: expose them only through iter_rows, never into the model. Test against a hand-written synthetic export in toolkit/tests/fixtures/parse/vcs/.

sources/accdb.py: accdb and mdb design read through the Jackcess bridge that S2.reference builds. Import exactly toolkit.reference.bridge and use only its start_jvm, open_database, tables, columns (name, neutral type, size, required; type unsupported:<DataType> when it cannot map one), iter_rows, queries and connect; until it is importable, parse exits 2 with 'accdb and mdb sources need the Jackcess bridge from S2.reference'.

`toolkit parse <eng> --strict --out DIR [--fail-on compiled-only,missing-backend,multi-backend,unresolved-link]`. --strict exits 1 on any parse error or unknown design part; warnings never fail. compiled-only: no VBA source (.accde, .mde or source.compiled_only). missing-backend: a linked back end that was not received (neither source.data_copy nor a source.backends entry names an existing file): exit 1. multi-backend: tables linked to more than one data back end: exit 2 with 'more than one data back end: custom quote' (an engagement has exactly one, source.data_copy). unresolved-link: a linked table whose connect string cannot be classified (Access back end, ODBC, SharePoint, Excel, text). The --fail-on conditions are checked after the model is written, so S0.healthcheck can still report them; S0.parse's own acceptance runs parse without --fail-on and the S0 exit criterion enforces it. Without --fail-on, parse models what the front end holds of the linked tables, so the free health check runs on a split app whose back end was not sent; the S2 and S3 prepare lists run parse with --fail-on missing-backend. When source.data_copy is set, compare the design tables, columns and types with the data copy through the Jackcess bridge and print per-table counts only; under --strict any difference exits 1. Whatever --fail-on says, parse exits 2 with 'encrypted source: custom quote' when the source file or a back end is encrypted or password-protected (no Jackcess codec is pinned and the bridge takes no password). Under MP_QUIET the summary holds counts per object kind, warning codes with counts and output paths, never text from the source.

scrub.py and `toolkit scrub` (decisions D8): before parse writes the model, replace connect-string credentials (PWD=, Password=, UID=), email addresses, phone numbers, credential URLs (scheme://user:password@host) and secret-like strings (private-key headers, AWS-style access keys, api_key, token and secret assignments) in every model string with typed tokens <SECRET-n>, <EMAIL-n>, <PHONE-n> and <URL-n>. The same original gets the same token within an engagement. The map goes to the private scrub-map.json. `toolkit scrub --check DIR` exits 1 naming file and JSON path, never the value, when anything remains.
Data-zone writes (workbook/ and scrub-map.json) are atomic (temp file, then os.replace), so concurrent reviewer runs are safe.

The xlsm fixture is built with openpyxl at test time; its VBA path is tested with hand-written PROJECT stream and module text (no binary vbaProject.bin is committed).

build: Format (docs/contracts.md#dataset-directory): <dir>/dataset.json plus <dir>/tables/<file-safe table>.csv (file-safe names per the contracts conventions). CSV: UTF-8 without BOM, RFC 4180 (comma, quoting only when needed, CRLF record ends), header row = the original column names in schema order. NULL is \N; an empty field is the empty string; a text that is exactly \N (or more backslashes then N) gets one extra leading backslash, which readers strip. datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (no zone, no fraction; date-only values get T00:00:00); yesno 1/0; byte, integer, longinteger and autonumber plain integers; currency and decimal plain with '.', no exponent, no thousands separator; single the shortest decimal that round-trips through IEEE binary32; double Python repr; NaN and infinity are errors; guid lower-case 8-4-4-4-12 without braces; text, memo and hyperlink as stored. complex and oleobject columns are omitted and listed in omitted_columns. dataset.json: format_version 1, name (engagement or seed-N), kind (engagement or synthetic), seed (null for engagement), schema_sha256 (SHA-256 of the schema.json bytes), load_order (every table, parents before children by schema.json relationships; cycles broken by name order and reported), tables [{name, file, rows, sha256 of the CSV bytes, columns [{name, type}] in schema order, omitted_columns [{name, type, reason complex|oleobject|computed}]}].

harness/dataset.py: read_dataset(dir) returning the metadata and, per table, an iterator of rows typed by the column types; write_dataset(dir, meta, tables); validate(dir, schema); and format_value(column type, value), the one implementation of the contracts dataset-directory text form (toolkit.dataset re-exports it, and stage1's per-table digests use it). Stdlib only; it must not import toolkit.

toolkit/dataset.py: adapters over the toolkit.sources readers: accdt sampleData XML; xlsm ListObjects with business data only (tables with role documentation are left out and calculated columns are omitted with reason computed; InvoiceGenerator exports InvoiceTable and CustomerTable); vcs-export table data files; CSV dataset directories; source.data_copy and accdb or mdb sources through the Jackcess bridge from S2.reference when it is importable (import exactly toolkit.reference.bridge and use only the functions S0.parse's sources/accdb.py names), otherwise exit 2 with 'data_copy needs the Jackcess bridge from S2.reference' (report blocked with that request). An engagement has no data when source.kind is accdt or vcs-export, saved_with_data is not true and data_copy is null: export then writes a dataset.json with an empty tables list and exits 0 with status ok, counts tables 0 and the message 'no data in the source' (S0 must pass for a health check on a design-only file; S2 and S3 refuse such an engagement in the driver). One data back end: export reads source.data_copy (or the source itself when it holds the data); tables linked to any other back end make export exit 2 with 'more than one data back end: custom quote'. Tables of a back end that was not received (neither source.data_copy nor a source.backends entry names an existing file) are skipped with status no-data, as for a design-only source: they are left out of dataset.json (tables and load_order), the rest is written, and export exits 0 with summary status no-data, its messages giving the number of skipped tables (docs/contracts.md#dataset-directory). toolkit.dataset.open_backend(path, schema) returns a reader with tables() and iter_rows(table) for an Access back-end file at any path, through the Jackcess bridge (exit 2 with the bridge request until S2.reference provides it); stage1 --dataset fresh-copy calls it.

`toolkit dataset export <eng> --out DIR [--check]`: writes the directory atomically (temp dir, then rename over DIR), validates what it wrote and exits 1 if it is invalid. --check regenerates into a temp dir, compares with DIR file by file and exits 1 on any difference, writing nothing. Summary: per-table row counts, sha256s and column names; never values.

`toolkit dataset validate <dir> --schema <schema.json>`: checks dataset.json against toolkit/schemas/dataset.schema.json, every table and column against the schema, the CSV rules, row counts and sha256s; prints counts only. A table may leave out a computed column when dataset.json lists it in omitted_columns with reason computed, and a table whose schema role is documentation may be absent: that is how synthetic seeds of an xlsm source look (S2.synth). It is used on synthetic seeds and fixtures; the engagement dataset is checked by export --check through mp-data.

Tests: round-trip every neutral type, including NULL versus the empty string, quotes, commas and newlines inside values, datetime, currency, single and double, yesno, omitted complex and oleobject columns, FK load order and a cycle; validate accepting an omitted computed column and an absent documentation table but rejecting an omitted ordinary column; format_value against the CSV writer; a hand-written accdt sampleData fixture; an xlsm workbook built with openpyxl at test time. Fixtures: toolkit/tests/fixtures/dataset/sample/ (a hand-written two-table dataset) and toolkit/tests/fixtures/dataset/schema.json.

build: inventory.py counts from the model only, never from the source. Access keys exactly as in northwind expected_inventory: tables, queries, queries_design_grid, queries_sql_text, forms, reports, modules, class_modules, macros, data_macro_files (only template/database/objects/dataMacros/*.axl; the 55 objects/properties/*.axl are metadata), data_macros, objects_with_code_behind, vba_nonblank_lines (non-blank lines not starting with 'Attribute ' in standard and class modules plus the CodeBehindForm and CodeBehindReport sections). Access also counts embedded_macros (macros embedded in form and report event properties); macros keeps counting standalone macro objects, so Northwind's expected_inventory still matches, and the extra key passes --expect. Inventory objects of type macro include the embedded ones, named <form>.<event> or <report>.<event>. vcs-export uses the Access keys; accdb and mdb count tables and queries only (a key a kind cannot provide is left out, never 0). xlsm keys exactly as in invoicegen expected_inventory: worksheets, hidden_worksheets, chartsheets, tables, table_columns, calculated_columns, defined_names (every definedName including _xlnm.*), defined_names_broken, data_validations, formula_cells, formula_cells_by_sheet, formula_cells_without_cached_value, array_formula_cells, charts, form_buttons, macro_assignments, activex_controls, cell_comments, vba_components, vba_standard_modules, vba_class_modules, vba_document_modules, vba_userforms, vba_nonblank_lines, vba_procedures, userform_controls, vba_references and sample_outputs.

inventory.json also holds the objects (every table, Access local or linked and xlsm ListObjects, as type table; calculated columns <Table>[<Column>]; formula blocks and data validations <Sheet>!<A1 range>; the other types and name forms as in docs/contracts.md#inventory, which rules.json sources[].type uses), per-object metrics (lines, procedures, controls, events, joins, parameters), dependency edges (query to tables, queries and functions; form or report to record source and procedures; procedure to tables, queries and forms; xlsm formula block to tables and names; button to macro), rule_bearing_kinds (Access: procedure, data_macro, macro, query, form, report; xlsm: procedure, userform, calculated_column, formula_block, data_validation, chart) and facts for the health check and the Stage 1 estimate (source and data-copy bytes, the number of data back ends, the number of relationships, linked tables by back-end kind, external links by kind, compiled_only, VBA present, and for xlsm the VBA references to Outlook or Word and the broken defined names). inventory.json also carries rate_usd_per_hour, the engagement's commercial.rate_usd_per_hour (null when unset), for estimate and the health check. Output is sorted and has no timestamps; parent directories are created.

--expect: when the engagement's expected_inventory has numeric keys, compare (keys starting with _ are ignored; nested objects are compared key by key; an expected key that is not counted fails; extra counted keys are listed but pass). Otherwise compare with the records inventory.lock.json. Otherwise write that lock (format_version 1, recorded date, source_sha256, counts) and exit 0 with status recorded, the message 'recorded, not compared; approve at the gate' and expectation recorded. Any difference exits 1, listing key, expected and counted; so does a lock whose source_sha256 differs from the engagement's source.sha256 (the pin, or source.lock.json through the loader; inventory never reads the source file). A missing model exits 2.

estimate.py, estimate.toml and `toolkit estimate <inventory.json> [--rules <rules.json>] [--delta <sha256>] --out <file.json>`. estimate.toml starts with `_source = "starting guesses, not measured; hours are your hours for the whole offer, comparable with pricing_tiers hours; change them only by a pipeline PR after at least 3 engagements (docs/runbook.md section 3, Recalibration)"`. Starting coefficients in estimate.toml (hours): base 24; per form 1.0, report 0.75, query 0.25, table 0.25, macro 0.25 (standalone and embedded), data macro 0.5, 100 VBA lines 0.75; xlsm per userform 1.5, formula block 0.5, calculated column 0.25, chart 0.5, data validation 0.1, business table 0.5, sample output kind 2.0. A [stage1] table prices Stage 1 for Access kinds: base 10, per table 0.15, per relationship 0.05, per linked or external link 0.25, per data macro 0.25. low = 0.8 x point, high = 1.25 x point. They change only as the Recalibration block of docs/runbook.md section 3 says. estimate.json is deterministic (sorted keys, no timestamps), so S1 can compare a fresh run with cmp: format_version 1, inventory_sha256, rules_sha256, hours {low, point, high}, tier, rate_usd_per_hour, price_usd {low, point, high}, price_note, stage1, by_area, delta, coefficients_sha256. rate_usd_per_hour is the engagement's commercial.rate_usd_per_hour (from inventory.json), else pipeline.json pricing.rate_usd_per_hour. price_usd applies the pipeline.json pricing rule (ceil(hours x rate / round_to_usd) x round_to_usd) to each of low, point and high; point is then clamped to the price_usd range of the tier row, and price_note names any clamp (null when there is none); when tier is not a single row of pricing_tiers (between rows, above stage2-standard, custom quote), nothing is clamped and price_note says why (docs/contracts.md#records). stage1, for Access kinds (else null), is {hours {low, point, high}, price_usd {low, point, high}} from the [stage1] table by the same rule, with point clamped to the stage1 tier row. With --delta, delta.price_usd prices the summed delta hours by the same rule, unclamped. tier is the Stage 2 row of pipeline.json pricing_tiers whose hours range holds the point estimate (stage2-small up to 90 h, including estimates under its 50 h floor; stage2-standard from 110 h); between 90 and 110 h it is 'between stage2-small and stage2-standard: decide at S1'; above 200 h 'above stage2-standard: split into phases'; with more than one data back end the tier is 'custom quote: more than one data back end'. --out creates parent directories.

--rules <rules.json> adds by_area hours from the kept objects of each area (rules.json objects[].area with decision keep). --delta <sha256> finds the committed version of the --rules file whose SHA-256 equals it (`git log --format=%H -- <file>` in its repo, then `git show <commit>:<path>`), prices only the added and changed rules, and writes the hours difference by area plus the added, removed and changed rule ids; it exits 2 when no committed version matches. `estimate render <estimate.json> --into <quote.md> [--check]` replaces only the block between <!-- estimate:begin --> and <!-- estimate:end -->; without --check it exits 2 when the markers are missing; with --check it writes nothing and exits 1 on a missing marker or any difference.

healthcheck.py and templates/docs/health-check.md (string.Template). `toolkit healthcheck <inventory.json> --out <md> [--check]` renders: a title with the project name; '## Size' (counts table); '## Risk flags', each with its trigger: source or data file above 1 GB (near the 2 GB Access file limit), split front end and back end or linked Access tables (multi-user use over a file share), VBA present (Office blocks macros in files from the internet), external links by kind (ODBC, SharePoint, Excel, text), compiled-only source, more than one data back end ('custom quote': an engagement has one data back end), linked Access tables with no data copy (facts.data_copy_bytes null: 'back end not received: the counts cover the front end only'), and for xlsm Outlook or Word automation in the VBA references and broken defined names; '## Complexity' (high when vba_nonblank_lines > 5000 or forms plus reports (xlsm: userforms plus formula blocks) > 40, medium when > 1000 lines or > 20 objects, else low; plus the 10 largest objects by lines, by name); '## Effort and price band' (hours low to high with price_usd low to high next to them, and the pricing_tiers row with its price range, or 'custom quote' with its reason; for Access kinds the Stage 1 band, stage1 hours and price_usd, next to the Stage 2 band); '## Next step' (the paid assessment from pricing_tiers, credited toward the migration, or, for Access kinds, Stage 1 alone). No generation date, no private paths and no data values. --check renders in memory and exits 1 on any difference.

Tests: counts on fixture models in toolkit/tests/fixtures/inventory/ (an Access model whose properties .axl are not counted as data macros; an xlsm model with every key); the three --expect branches; inventory objects of type table and the xlsm name forms; estimate with --rules, --delta (a temporary git repo with two committed rules.json versions; an unknown sha exits 2) and render --into replacing only the marked block, plus --check (exit 1 on a difference and on missing markers); two estimate runs give identical bytes; price_usd by the pricing rule, its rounding to round_to_usd and the clamp of point with price_note; the stage1 band of an Access model; delta.price_usd unclamped; the custom-quote tier and risk flag for two data back ends; health check rendering and --check.

gate.name: Assessment signed
client: Assessment run only (no args.change_order): Send the client {{p.records}}/quote.md as a file, and analysis/rules.md and analysis/keep-drop.md as files when target.mode is local, otherwise as links to the files on the target S1 branch.

Go through the open questions with the client (change-order run: only the questions the change order added). Record each answer under its `## Q-<area>-NNN` heading in {{p.records}}/answers.md with `answered: YYYY-MM-DD` and `by: client`. Write rules, never data values.

If an answer changes a rule, re-run S1 before signing as docs/runbook.md section 2(j) describes: the launcher regenerated with --prior, which embeds prior and prior_items from {{p.records}}/runs/S1.json (change-order run: runs/S1-CO-NNN.json), and in args-S1.json the next attempt, items from the S1.areas items_from cmd (section 2(e)), rerun ["S1.synthesize"] plus "S1.area.<area id>" for each affected area, and since naming the answered question ids.

Assessment run only (no args.change_order): The client signs the sign-off block on a PDF of analysis/rules.md and accepts the fixed price in quote.md. Do not edit the committed analysis files to add the signature.

Assessment run only (no args.change_order): Record the approval in {{p.records}}/gates.json as "S1": {approved, signed_by, rules_sha256, rules_md_sha256, deposit_received}, with the two hashes from `sha256sum {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.md` at the head of the target S1 branch. rules.json keeps `signed: null`: the signature is recorded only in gates.json, never in a committed file. spec-check in the S2, S4, S5 and S6 exit criteria compares the files with these hashes.

Assessment run only (no args.change_order): In {{p.records}}/engagement.json set commercial.quote (the fixed price before credit), commercial.assessment_credit_usd (the assessment price paid, null when none) and commercial.budget_hours (hours.point in {{p.records}}/estimate.json), and add every newly sold offer to commercial.purchased. When stage1 or a stage2 offer is sold while target.mode is local, switch the engagement to github as pipeline docs/runbook.md 1.6 says before the next stage's 2(a); the driver refuses those stages in local mode.

Assessment run only (no args.change_order): Invoice the assessment (100% at this gate). If Stage 2 is sold, invoice the 30% deposit and set deposit_received to true only once it is paid; the driver refuses S2 before that.

Change-order run only: the client approves {{p.records}}/change-orders/CO-NNN.md and its price. Set `approved: YYYY-MM-DD` in its header, record "CO-NNN": {approved, rules_sha256, rules_md_sha256} in gates.json with the hashes from the same sha256sum at the head of the target S1 branch, add the change order's hours to commercial.budget_hours, then invoice it. Until then spec-check prints 'pending CO-NNN: approve at the gate' and exits 0.

If the client buys nothing more (assessment is the last purchased offer): the retention end date is this gate's date plus data_policy.retention_days_after_acceptance. Note it in the S1 row of {{p.records}}/log.md, run `mp-data purge {{p.records}}/engagement.json --dry-run` in a plain terminal now, and run it without --dry-run on that date (pipeline docs/runbook.md section 7).
Squash-merge the S1 PRs only after gates.json is recorded (target.mode local: squash-merge the target S1 branch into main locally). After signature, rules change only through a change order.
Log your gate and review minutes in the S1 row of {{p.records}}/log.md.

build: rules.schema.json, format_version 1, as in contracts.md#rules-json. Top level: format_version, kind (area|merged), engagement, spec_version (a string matching ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$: "1.0" from S1.synthesize, and each S1.change_order raises the minor part to 1.1, 1.2 and so on), areas, rules, objects, lookups, relations, workflows, services, open_questions, signed (null, or {by, date, rules_md_sha256, rules_json_sha256} only in a copy handed to the client). areas[]: id ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,29}$, title, status kept|dropped, queries, forms, reports, procedures, tables. rules[]: id ^R-<area>-[0-9]{3}$, area, statement, trigger, sources[{type, ref}] (type is an inventory object type, ref an inventory object name), tables, confidence high|medium|low, test_kind rule|equivalence|e2e, questions. objects[]: type, name, decision keep|drop|out_of_scope, area, target_component (required for keep), reason (required for drop and out_of_scope). Object types and names are exactly the inventory's (contracts.md#inventory): tables are type `table`, procedures `<module>.<procedure>` (xlsm `<component>.<procedure>`), data macros `<table>.<event>`, calculated columns `<Table>[<Column>]`, formula blocks and data validations `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`, charts `<Sheet>!<chart name>`. lookups[{table, column, copy_values, values, rule}] where values is null, or a list of unique non-empty code strings (allowed only with copy_values true). relations[{table, fk, on_delete CASCADE|PROTECT|SET_NULL|DO_NOTHING, rule}], workflows[{id, title, forms, reports, rules, steps}], services[{name, area, inputs, outputs, errors}], open_questions[{id ^Q-<area>-[0-9]{3}$, text, status open|answered}]. No other keys (additionalProperties false).

`toolkit rules-lint FILE`: jsonschema validation, then semantic checks, each reported with its JSON pointer: ids unique; every rule id's <area> equals its area and that area exists; area ids are not Python keywords and not in pipeline.json item_ids.reserved; every question id cited by a rule exists in open_questions; every rule id cited by lookups, relations and workflows exists; a kept area has at least one object with decision keep and a dropped area has none; each object (type, name) appears once; objects and sources of type calculated_column match `<Table>[<Column>]`, and of type formula_block or data_validation match `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`; every rule with test_kind e2e is listed in at least one workflows[].rules; lookups[].values is non-null only with copy_values true; a kind area file holds exactly one area and only its rules, objects and questions; signed is null in every file it lints (committed files never hold the signature: it lives in gates.json).

`toolkit rules-coverage RULES INVENTORY --require PCT`: the denominator is every inventory object whose type is in inventory.json rule_bearing_kinds plus every table. An object is covered when it appears exactly once in objects[] and, if it is kept and rule-bearing, at least one rule cites it in sources or its reason says why it holds no rule. Hard failures, whatever the percentage: an objects[] entry or a sources ref that is not in the inventory, and duplicates. Prints covered/total, the percentage with one decimal and the uncovered object names (names only). Exit 0 when the percentage is at least PCT and there is no hard failure.

`toolkit rules-render RULES --keep-drop MD [--check]`: writes keep-drop.md deterministically from rules.json, as contracts.md#rules-json describes: a first line saying it is generated from analysis/rules.json and must not be edited by hand, then one table each for Keep, Drop and Out of scope (type, name, area, target component or reason), sorted by area, type and name. With --check it renders in memory, prints the first differing line numbers and exits 1 on any difference; it never writes.

`toolkit spec-check ANALYSIS --gates GATES --change-orders DIR`: hashes ANALYSIS/rules.json and ANALYSIS/rules.md (sha256 of the raw bytes). The approved state is gates.json S1 {rules_sha256, rules_md_sha256}, replaced by the highest-numbered gates.json CO-NNN entry that has approved set. Exit 0 when both hashes equal the approved state. Also exit 0, printing 'pending CO-NNN: approve at the gate', when they equal rules_sha256_after and rules_md_sha256_after in the header of the highest-numbered DIR/CO-NNN.md that has no approved gates.json entry and whose base_rules_sha256 equals the approved rules_sha256. Header lines start at column 0 in the form `base_rules_sha256: <hex>`, `rules_sha256_after: <hex>` and `rules_md_sha256_after: <hex>` (contracts.md#records). A missing DIR means no change orders, not an error: S2 to S6 run spec-check on engagements that never had one. Exit 1 otherwise, including 'spec not signed' when gates.json has no S1 rules_sha256; exit 2 when rules.json, rules.md or GATES is missing. Prints hashes and the matched state only.

data-model.schema.json for analysis/data-model.json (xlsm only): format_version 1, source_kind "xlsm", tables and relationships in exactly the toolkit/schemas/model.schema.json shapes (reuse its definitions by $ref, or copy them if it has no $defs), plus mappings[{list_object, source_column, table, column, line}] (line is the repeating-group index such as 1..3, else null), computed[{list_object, source_column, rule}] for calculated columns that are not stored, and dropped_tables[{list_object, reason}] for documentation tables. `toolkit schema-lint FILE`: jsonschema validation, then table and column names snake_case and unique, types in the neutral list from contracts.md#object-model, primary keys and relationship columns exist, every mapping target exists, and no source column is both mapped and computed.

Fixtures in toolkit/tests/fixtures/rules/, all invented (a small book-lending app: tables Member, Book, Loan, Fine; queries, a form, a report, a procedure and a data macro): valid.json (merged, with one lookup that carries values, one rule of each test_kind, the e2e one listed in a workflow, and one kept rule-bearing object that no rule cites but whose reason says why it holds no rule), valid-area.json, one invalid-*.json per lint rule (invalid-area-id.json uses a kebab-case id; invalid-signed.json has a signed object), inventory.json (Access-style, with rule_bearing_kinds and every table as type table), valid-xlsm.json and inventory-xlsm.json (table, calculated_column named `<Table>[<Column>]`, formula_block and data_validation named `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`, userform, chart objects), keep-drop.md rendered from valid.json, data-model.json plus invalid variants, and analysis/{rules.json,rules.md}, gates.json (S1 hashes and one approved CO-NNN entry) and change-orders/ (one approved and one pending change order) for spec-check.

It also runs the jq programs of pipeline.json S1.areas and S5.features items_from (read from pipeline.json, run with the jq binary on valid.json), checks the expected ids, titles and scope strings, and checks that the S5.features program is identical to the one in docs/contracts.md#rules-json. test_spec_check.py: signed state passes; an edited rules.json fails; a pending change order with the right base passes and prints 'pending'; one with a wrong base fails; an approved CO-NNN entry becomes the new state; a missing change-orders directory passes on the signed state; no S1 entry fails with 'spec not signed'; a missing gates.json exits 2.

tasks.title: Recover business rules per functional area
tasks.scout: Split the application into functional areas for rule recovery. Read only {{p.private}}/out/inventory.json and {{p.private}}/out/model/ (the design zone). Every object whose type is listed in inventory.json rule_bearing_kinds, and every table, goes into exactly one area. Return at most 4 items; merge areas rather than exceed 4. Hinted areas (use these ids where they fit): {{e.scope.areas_hint}}. Must keep: {{e.scope.must_keep}}. Handled by the foundation (S4), not an area of its own: {{e.scope.foundation}}; put the objects that implement it in the area that uses them most. Documentation sheets, switchboards and start-up forms also go in the area that uses them most. An embedded macro (`<form>.<event>` or `<report>.<event>`) goes in the area of its form or report. Look for behaviour that runs on a schedule (an AutoExec macro or other startup action, a form Timer event, an Application.OnTime call): it holds rules with a `schedule:<when>` trigger, so put the objects that hold it in the area whose tables it changes. Item id: snake_case matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,29}$, not a Python keyword, not the app package name {{e.app.slug}}, unique, and not one of users, contrib, static, templates, utils, legacy, core, domain, tests, e2e, rules, config, admin, auth, sessions, account, socialaccount, mfa; it becomes the Django app name in S5. title: a short business name. scope: one string listing every object of the area as 'type: name' with the type and name exactly as in inventory.json, separated by ', '. Put any object you cannot place in uncovered; the stage is blocked unless uncovered is empty.

items_from.jq: . as $r | [.areas[] | {id, title, scope: (.id as $a | [$r.objects[] | select(.area == $a) | .type + ": " + .name] | join(", "))}]

Scope: {{item.scope}}. Paraphrase; never copy code, SQL, expressions or form text. Use scrubbed tokens such as <SECRET-1> or <EMAIL-3> as they are; never ask for or reconstruct the original values. Read only {{p.private}}/out/; never open the data zone.

Object types and names exactly as in inventory.json (contracts.md#inventory): every table as type `table`; procedures `<module>.<procedure>` (xlsm `<component>.<procedure>`); data macros `<table>.<event>`; calculated columns `<Table>[<Column>]`; formula blocks and data validations `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`; charts `<Sheet>!<chart name>`. S2 maps equivalence units to areas and decisions by these names.

test_kind by how S5 proves the rule: `rule` gets one test in app/{{e.app.slug}}/{{item.id}}/tests/test_rules.py (S5.features); `equivalence` is proven by the equivalence units of its sources (a query, a calculated column, a formula block, or a procedure that writes a document); `e2e` is proven by S5.e2e and must be listed in a workflows[].rules entry

lookups[]: copy_values true only when the codes are behaviour. S2.synth copies codes from the design (value lists, list validations, literals in criteria or code) and, only when the design holds none, from the lookup's `values`.
