tasks.title: Review the assessment
lenses: Source fidelity: in each area pick at least 5 rules (all of them when an area has fewer) and try to refute each against the design model in {{p.private}}/out/model/ (procedures and events, data macros, queries; for a workbook its formulas, calculated columns, validations, userforms and macros). Look for behaviour in rule-bearing objects that no rule covers, and check that statements are paraphrased, with no copied code, SQL, expressions or form text. Read only {{p.private}}/out/.

Spec and quote quality: every rule is testable, unambiguous and has the right test_kind (`rule`: one test in the area's tests/test_rules.py in S5; `equivalence`: its sources produce equivalence units; `e2e`: listed in a workflow); object names follow the inventory (tables type `table`, calculated columns `<Table>[<Column>]`, formula blocks `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`); every copy_values lookup whose codes are not in the design (value lists, list validations, literals in criteria or code) carries `values` from answers.md or an open question, never codes from data; rules.json has signed null; must_keep items ({{e.scope.must_keep}}) are kept and keep-drop.md names their components; foundation items ({{e.scope.foundation}}) are not areas; area ids are valid Django app names and equal the area files' ids; interfaces.md is target-neutral; every open question has an id and an answers.md heading; for xlsm, data-model.json maps every business ListObject column or lists it as computed, with repeating groups normalised; estimate.json and the quote's hours, tier and risks are consistent with the inventory and pipeline.json pricing_tiers; for a change order, no id is reused or renumbered and the delta prices only added or changed rules.

tasks.title: Reference engine for Access: query designs to Access SQL, run on UCanAccess
inputs: {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json (objects with decision keep, rules that cite app functions)
reuse: UCanAccess 5.1.8 (Apache-2.0) as the engine
Jackcess 5.1.7: io.github.spannm.jackcess.impl.query.QueryImpl as the design-to-SQL formatter, and its DatabaseBuilder, Database and Column API for the bridge
JPype1 1.7.1 for one in-process JVM
toolkit.dataset (S0.dataset) to read dataset directories
toolkit.engagement.load and toolkit.quiet (S0.workspace)
tasks.goal: Turn every saved query into Access SQL and run it on the UCanAccess reference engine against this engagement's data and against any synthetic seed, so goldens can be recorded without Access or Windows.
deliverables: {{p.private}}/out/reference/catalog.json and out/reference/sql/ (design zone: derived only from the scrubbed model): one unit per saved query with its Access SQL, object {type: query, name}, depends_on, params, app_functions, needs_access_confirmation, status (ok, needs-params or unsupported) and a reason from the contract enum (action-query, crosstab, form-reference-unresolved, unsupported-function, pass-through, other)

`mp-data reference build --dataset engagement` writes only {{p.private}}/reference/engagement.accdb (data zone: a private copy of source.data_copy when it is set, or of the source file for kind accdb or mdb with layout single-file, else built from {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement). `uv run toolkit reference build --dataset seeds` writes {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/seed-N.accdb (design zone: built only from the model and {{p.target}}/goldens/synthetic/seed-N/input). The engagement build fails when every engagement table has 0 rows, unless the engagement declares no data

Every app-defined VBA function that a kept query calls is available to the engine: a correlated-subquery rewrite in {{p.target}}/goldens/reference/functions/<Function>.json that cites its rule id, or, only when reusable across engagements, Java in java/, which start_jvm compiles into a temp jar at each JVM start. The choice per function is in notes
`reference run --summary` runs every ok unit read-only and prints counts per status and rows per unit, never values (summary `units` [{id, status, reason, dataset, total}], total = rows returned)

ReferenceAdapter in toolkit/commands/reference.py (the adapter protocol from docs/contracts.md#harness plus describe(unit_id)), dispatching on source.kind; S2.golden and `equivalence --adapter reference` use it

toolkit.reference.bridge, an importable Jackcess and UCanAccess bridge. S0's sources/accdb.py (accdb and mdb design) and toolkit/dataset.py (rows from source.data_copy and from accdb or mdb files; S3's `stage1 --dataset fresh-copy` reads them through toolkit.dataset) import it; until it exists they exit 2 with a named request

`python -m toolkit.reference.qbe <eng>` prints each saved query's id and the SQL the formatter makes from its design, reading only {{p.private}}/out/model/ and writing nothing. Reviewers use it to check SQL against designs

Tests in toolkit/tests/test_reference.py on hand-written synthetic fixtures, and toolkit/tests/test_bridge_sources.py, which proves S0's accdb, mdb and data_copy readers (`toolkit parse`, `dataset export`) on databases it creates through the bridge
acceptance: uv run ruff check toolkit/reference toolkit/commands/reference.py toolkit/tests/test_reference.py toolkit/tests/test_bridge_sources.py
uv run python -c "from toolkit.reference.bridge import start_jvm, open_database, tables, columns, iter_rows, queries, connect"

build: toolkit/reference/bridge.py, the importable module toolkit.reference.bridge. S0.parse (sources/accdb.py) and S0.dataset (toolkit/dataset.py) import it, and S3.move reaches it through toolkit.dataset. Importing it starts nothing and imports nothing else from toolkit.reference; JPype1 is imported inside the functions. start_jvm(): start one JVM per process with JPype1 from $JAVA_HOME (set in the env file by the jdk environment item), or do nothing when it is running. Classpath: the three jars that `uv run toolkit fetch --jars` put in vendor/ (ucanaccess 5.1.8, jackcess 5.1.7, hsqldb 2.7.4). When java/ has sources, start_jvm first compiles them with $JAVA_HOME/bin/javac (ucanaccess jar on the classpath) into a jar in a new directory under tempfile.gettempdir(), which follows $TMPDIR, adds that jar to the classpath and removes the directory at exit. It never writes under the toolkit root: vendor/ is gitignored and only fetch restores it, and the root is read-only inside mp-data's jail and in a pinned release (docs/contracts.md#data-plane-jail). The JVM also gets -Djava.io.tmpdir set to tempfile.gettempdir(), because Java ignores $TMPDIR and the jail keeps /tmp read-only. JPype cannot restart a JVM, so the classpath is fixed at the first start. No other runtime jar is needed (jackcess declares poi as optional). open_database(path, read_only=True): a Jackcess Database opened with DatabaseBuilder. tables(db): user table names (no MSys tables). columns(db, table): (name, neutral type, size, required) per column, mapping Jackcess DataType to the neutral types of docs/contracts.md#object-model (autonumber from Column.isAutoNumber(), hyperlink from Column.isHyperlink()); a type with no neutral match is returned as unsupported:<DataType name> for the caller to report. iter_rows(db, table): row tuples of Python values (int, Decimal, float, str, bool, datetime, None), with complex and OLE columns as None. queries(db): (name, type, Access SQL) per saved query, from Database.getQueries() and toSQLString(). connect(path, read_only=True, memory=True, new_version=None): a UCanAccess JDBC connection; new_version V2010 or V2003 sets newDatabaseVersion, so a missing file is created in that format (`reference build` and the tests create databases this way). A missing JAVA_HOME or jar raises an error that names the jdk environment item or `uv run toolkit fetch --jars` (under MP_SANDBOX=mp-data, where the toolkit root is read-only: `mp-data fetch <eng> --verify`, which restores the jars of the root mp-data runs); commands turn it into exit 2. vendor/ belongs to each toolkit root: for clients mp-data runs the pinned release, so its fetch never fills the pipeline worktree's vendor/, and the S0, S1 and S2 prepare lists run `uv run toolkit fetch --jars` for the worktree's `uv run` commands and tests

toolkit/reference/qbe.py: turn each parsed query design in model/objects.json into a list of QueryImpl.Row(id=null, attribute, expression, flag, extra, name1, name2, objectId, order). Get Access SQL from QueryImpl.create(objectFlag, name, rows, objectId).toSQLString(). Emit attribute 0 START, 1 TYPE, 2 PARAMETER (one row per declared parameter), 3 FLAG, 5 InputTables, 6 OutputColumns, 7 Joins, 8 Where, 9 Groups, 10 Having, 11 OrderBy and 255 END rows. objectFlag is 0 for SELECT and 128 for UNION. SQL-text queries pass through unchanged. Action queries get status unsupported with reason action-query; crosstab and pass-through queries get their own reasons. `python -m toolkit.reference.qbe <eng>` loads the engagement with toolkit.engagement.load and prints, for every saved query in model/objects.json, its id and the generated SQL (or its status and reason). It reads only the design zone and writes nothing

`reference sql <eng> --all`: write {{p.private}}/out/reference/catalog.json (docs/contracts.md#reference-catalog; engine ucanaccess-5.1.8) and out/reference/sql/<file-safe id>.sql for every query in the model. These are design-zone files: they derive only from the scrubbed model, so agents and reviewers may read them. File-safe id (docs/contracts.md conventions): each character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] becomes _, and when anything was replaced, append - and the first 8 hex digits of sha256 of the id in UTF-8 (`Order Details` becomes `Order_Details-fe3ac0d4`). Each unit has id = the query name, kind saved_query, object {type: query, name} (the rules.json object it implements), sql_ref, depends_on (queries it reads, in dependency order), params (declared parameters and Forms!/Reports! references, source form_control or prompt), app_functions, status, reason, and needs_access_confirmation: true when the SQL calls Format, FormatDateTime, DateValue, CDate, DatePart, DateDiff, DateAdd, Weekday, MonthName or an app function. Reads only the design zone. stdout: counts per status, plus the ids that are not ok with their reasons; under MP_QUIET=1 the summary carries `counts` and `units` [{id, status, reason}] (docs/contracts.md#summary-schema)

`reference build <eng> --dataset engagement|seeds|seed-N`: build each database in a temp file in its target directory, then rename it (a rename from $TMPDIR would cross mounts inside the jail). seeds = every seed-N directory under {{p.target}}/goldens/synthetic/. Two commands build the two zones, because mp-data runs its toolkit child with only the data zone, $TMPDIR and the declared outputs writable (docs/contracts.md#data-plane-jail). `uv run toolkit reference build <eng> --dataset seeds|seed-N` reads only the design zone and committed seeds, runs the `reference sql` step first when out/reference/catalog.json is missing or older than the model, and writes {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/seed-N.accdb (design zone). `mp-data reference build <eng> --dataset engagement` writes only {{p.private}}/reference/engagement.accdb (data zone), never the catalog or a seed database: it exits 2 naming `uv run toolkit reference sql <eng> --all` when out/reference/catalog.json is missing or older than the model. Every list that builds the engagement database runs the seeds build (or `reference sql`) on the line before. `--dataset all` exits 2 and names the two commands (`uv run toolkit reference build <eng> --dataset seeds`, then `mp-data reference build <eng> --dataset engagement`). For engagement with source.data_copy set, or kind accdb or mdb with layout single-file, make a private copy of that file. Otherwise (accdt or vcs-export without data_copy), and for every seed, create a new database with UCanAccess newDatabaseVersion=V2010, emit Access DDL from model/schema.json (docs/contracts.md#object-model types), and insert the rows of the dataset directory with toolkit.dataset: {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement, or {{p.target}}/goldens/synthetic/seed-N/input. A seed database never takes anything from the engagement files. Create the catalog's saved queries in dependency order so queries on queries resolve, in a new database and in a copy that lacks them (a back-end data_copy), and record how in notes (UCanAccess views or inlined derived tables). Skip a dataset whose database is newer than its dataset files and the catalog. Never an empty reference: when every engagement table has 0 rows, exit 1 with 'empty reference'. The only exception is an engagement that declares no data (kind accdt or vcs-export, source.saved_with_data not true and source.data_copy null, as toolkit.dataset defines it; the driver already refuses a design-only accdt before S2 and S3): then `--dataset engagement` exits 2 with 'no engagement data: set source.data_copy', and the seed databases build as usual. The summary carries counts only (databases built and skipped, tables, rows)

`reference run <eng> --dataset <name> --all --summary`: open the dataset's database (engagement: {{p.private}}/reference/engagement.accdb; seed-N: {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/seed-N.accdb) with readOnly=true and memory=true (parallel reviewers must not conflict), run every ok unit and print counts per status and the row count per unit. Write nothing. Under MP_QUIET=1 the summary carries `counts` per status and `units` [{id, status, reason, dataset, total}], where total is the unit's row count and a unit that returns 0 rows has status empty; never values. Seeds may run as `uv run toolkit reference run <eng> --dataset seed-N --all --summary` (design zone); the engagement dataset runs only through mp-data. Parameters come from {{p.private}}/goldens/params.json (engagement) or {{p.target}}/goldens/params.json (seeds) when present; before S2.golden has written them, parameterised units count as needs-params. A unit that fails at run time is reported with its Java exception class only and makes the command exit 1. Fix the translation, or make `reference sql` classify it with a reason from the enum. Never hand-edit catalog.json

App functions (Northwind: ProductAllocated, ProductOnOrder, ProductToSell, ProductNoStock): prefer rewriting each call as a correlated subquery. Write {{p.target}}/goldens/reference/functions/<Function>.json as {function, args, rewrite (SQL with {arg} placeholders), rule (the R- id it implements), choice: "subquery"}, paraphrased from the rules spec and never copied from VBA. The sql step substitutes the calls. Only a function that other engagements can reuse becomes Java in java/: methods annotated with @net.ucanaccess.ext.FunctionType(functionName, argumentTypes, returnType), compiled by start_jvm into its temp jar (above) and registered with UcanaccessConnection.addFunctions. A function that is neither gets status unsupported, reason unsupported-function, and a question in notes

ReferenceAdapter in toolkit/commands/reference.py, duck-typed to the protocol in docs/contracts.md#harness with no import from harness/. The harness plugin creates it with no arguments, so it finds the private directory in $EQUIVALENCE_PRIVATE (golden record may pass private= instead) and dispatches on the engine named in out/reference/catalog.json. load_dataset(dir) reads dir/dataset.json and opens that dataset's reference database read-only (readOnly=true, memory=true): engagement opens reference/engagement.accdb, seed-N opens synthetic/reference/seed-N.accdb. run_saved_query(unit_id, params) returns row tuples in output-column order. render_document raises NotImplementedError for Access. describe(unit_id) returns [(column, neutral type)] for golden record. The module dispatches sql, build, run and selfcheck on engagement source.kind, and ReferenceAdapter on the catalog engine, to toolkit.reference or toolkit.reference_xlsm, imported lazily so a missing package exits 2 with its name. selfcheck exists only for xlsm; for other kinds it exits 2 and says so

Tests (toolkit/tests/test_reference.py, fixtures in toolkit/tests/fixtures/reference/): hand-written synthetic designs for a join, an outer join, a group by with having, a declared parameter, a union, a query on a query and an app-function call rewrite. Expected SQL is written by hand; expected rows come from tiny synthetic tables loaded through `reference build` on a fixture dataset directory. Also test the empty-reference failure, that `--dataset engagement` refuses a missing or stale catalog and writes nothing outside reference/, that `--dataset all` exits 2, that two read-only opens can run at once, the file-safe id rule, and the bridge on a database the test creates with UCanAccess: tables, columns with neutral types, iter_rows values and queries, and that importing toolkit.reference.bridge starts no JVM. Test the java/ compile step (javac argv and output path) as a function: it writes only under the temp dir. Nothing is copied from Northwind

Tests of S0's readers on created sources (toolkit/tests/test_bridge_sources.py, fixtures in toolkit/tests/fixtures/reference/bridge_sources/). S0.parse and S0.dataset read accdb and mdb files and source.data_copy only through this bridge, which did not exist when their tests ran, so this test proves those paths on files it creates. Fixture: a hand-written dataset directory (dataset.json and tables/*.csv) with two related tables (text, integer, currency, datetime and yesno columns, a few rows each) and the matching text parts of an .accdt. In tmp_path, create an .accdb (newDatabaseVersion V2010) and an .mdb (V2003, Jackcess FileFormat.V2003) through toolkit.reference.bridge: connect(path, read_only=False, new_version=...), Access DDL for the fixture tables, and the rows read with toolkit.dataset. UCanAccess keeps views in its HSQLDB mirror and Jackcess has no query writer, so the test adds two saved queries (a SELECT with an inner join, and a UNION) to each file with open_database(path, read_only=False) and Database.getSystemTable: one MSysObjects row each (Type 5, Flags 0 for the SELECT and 128 for the UNION, a new Id) and their MSysQueries rows with the attributes qbe.py emits; queries(db) returns both. Each check uses a test engagement.json that make_engagement (toolkit/tests/conftest.py) writes under tmp_path. (1) `toolkit parse <eng> --strict --out DIR` with kind accdb on the .accdb and with kind mdb on the .mdb (layout single-file) exits 0; the MP_QUIET summary counts the 2 tables and 2 queries, and model/objects.json holds each query's Access SQL. (2) An .accdt assembled at test time from the fixture's text parts, with source.data_copy naming the created .accdb: parse --strict exits 0 (design and data copy match, per-table counts only); the same .accdt with one column's type changed exits 1. (3) `toolkit dataset export <eng> --out DIR` for that accdt engagement reads the data copy, and every table's rows in the written dataset.json equal the fixture's dataset.json. No client file, demo source or engagements/<id>/ record is read
reuse: vendor/ jars fetched by `uv run toolkit fetch --jars` (S0.workspace); this task never downloads jars
toolkit.dataset (S0.dataset) for reading dataset directories; do not write a second reader
toolkit.engagement.load for paths and toolkit.quiet for MP_QUIET output (S0.workspace)

tasks.title: Reference outputs for a workbook: recomputed formulas and shipped documents
inputs: {{p.private}}/out/model/ (schema.json with one table per ListObject, objects.json with formula blocks and defined names, procedures.json)
{{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json (objects with decision keep, rules for the document macros)
toolkit/reference/ and toolkit/commands/reference.py (the Access engine's catalog, CLI and adapter shape)
reuse: formualizer 0.11.1 (MIT) to recompute formulas
openpyxl 3.1.5 for table metadata, cell maps and writing seed rows
pypdf 6.20.1 for PDF text
olefile 0.47 (BSD) for .msg MAPI properties
toolkit.dataset (S0.dataset) to read dataset directories
LibreOffice headless only as an optional cross-check when `soffice` is on PATH
tasks.goal: Record what the workbook computes (every formula output) and what it produces (PDF, xlsx and email documents), for the shipped data and for synthetic seeds, behind the same `reference` commands and adapter as the Access engine.
deliverables: {{p.private}}/out/reference/catalog.json (design zone; engine formualizer-0.11.1) with formula_output units (each calculated column as `<Table>[<Column>]`, each formula block outside tables as `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`) and document units invoice_pdf, invoice_xlsx and email_draft (docs/contracts.md#documents). Each unit names its rules.json object and has needs_access_confirmation false; params for input cells such as the dashboard as_of have source input_cell

Structured-reference to A1 rewrite before formualizer, and the seed recompute. `reference selfcheck --min-match 1.0` matches every formula cell of the shipped workbook with Excel's cached value (InvoiceGenerator: 335 of 335)

Seed workbooks {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/seed-N.xlsx (`uv run toolkit reference build --dataset seeds`) built only from the model and the committed seeds, never copied from the shipped workbook; the engagement copy is {{p.private}}/reference/engagement.xlsx (`mp-data reference build --dataset engagement`, which writes nothing else)

Document fields from the shipped outputs (3 PDFs, 3 Strict OOXML xlsx, 2 .msg). Seed documents are emulated from the macro spec and proved against the shipped outputs; the emulation spec is in {{p.target}}/goldens/reference/functions/documents.json
toolkit/commands/reference.py dispatches sql, build, run, selfcheck and ReferenceAdapter to toolkit.reference_xlsm for xlsm, and the Access tests stay green
LibreOffice cross-check when `soffice` is on PATH; otherwise notes say 'LibreOffice cross-check skipped: not available' (not blocking)
acceptance: uv run ruff check toolkit/reference_xlsm toolkit/commands/reference.py toolkit/tests/test_reference_xlsm.py

build: `reference sql` for xlsm: read model/schema.json and objects.json and write {{p.private}}/out/reference/catalog.json (engine formualizer-0.11.1). Write one formula_output unit per calculated column (id `<Table>[<Column>]`, rows keyed by the table's inferred key) and one per formula block outside tables (id `<Sheet>!<A1 range>`: dashboard KPIs, the monthly series, the Template cells). Write document units invoice_pdf, invoice_xlsx and email_draft, keyed by invoice number. Params come from input cells that formulas read (InvoiceGenerator: as_of = Dashboard!C1, name TODAY, type datetime, source input_cell). Each unit names its rules.json object: {type: calculated_column or formula_block, name}, or for a document {type: procedure, name} of the procedure that writes the file. needs_access_confirmation is false. Rewritten formulas go to out/reference/sql/<file-safe id>.txt, with the file-safe id rule of the Access engine (`InvoiceTable[Net Amount]` becomes `InvoiceTable_Net_Amount_-f34d32b9`). Broken #REF! names (Date_Chart, Value_Chart) are reported, not fatal

Structured-reference rewrite (required: formualizer 0.11.1 does not import ListObjects; measured on InvoiceGenerator, at most 16 of 335 cells match without the rewrite, even with the tables registered through add_table, and 335 of 335 with it). From openpyxl table metadata, rewrite Table[[#This Row],[Col]] to $<col><row> and Table[Col] to $<col>$<first>:$<col>$<last>, with a sheet prefix when the table is on another sheet. Leave all other text unchanged. A form the rewrite does not know makes the unit unsupported, reason unsupported-function

Recompute with formualizer (load_workbook, set_value for inputs, evaluate_all, evaluate_cell). Seeds (`uv run toolkit reference build --dataset seeds|seed-N`, as for Access): build {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/seed-N.xlsx with openpyxl from the design zone and the committed seed only. Never copy the shipped workbook there: it holds engagement values (cached results, constants, document text), and agents may read synthetic/. From {{p.private}}/out/model/, recreate the sheets that hold business ListObjects or formulas, each such ListObject (ref, headers, calculatedColumnFormula), the formula blocks, the defined names and the scrubbed label cells. Write the seed rows from {{p.target}}/goldens/synthetic/seed-N/input (original column names), resize table.ref, copy each calculatedColumnFormula into the new rows, rewrite, evaluate and read the outputs. A non-formula cell outside the tables that a formula reads is an input cell: a param of the units that read it (source input_cell), set at run time with set_value from the params that golden record chooses, never stored in the seed workbook. Engagement: the formula outputs are Excel's cached values (the oracle), and `mp-data reference build --dataset engagement` copies the workbook to {{p.private}}/reference/engagement.xlsx and writes nothing else; `--dataset all` exits 2 as for Access

`reference selfcheck <eng> --min-match 1.0`: recompute the shipped workbook from its own inputs and compare every formula cell with its cached value (a cell without a cached value compares as empty). Also run the document emulation on the shipped rows and compare it field by field with the fields extracted from the shipped PDFs, xlsx and .msg files. Work in memory and write nothing. build: harness/canonical.py (stdlib only, so it can be vendored; canonical_version 1 per docs/contracts.md#canonical-output). It formats values by the unit's neutral column types: UTF-8 CSV with a header, NULL as \N, integers plain, currency and decimal with 4 places, single to 6 significant digits, double to 12, datetime as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with no time zone, yes/no as 1/0, text in NFC. Row order: when the unit has an ORDER BY on output columns, sort by those columns (recorded in the manifest as order_by) and break ties by the full row tuple; otherwise sort by the full row tuple. Document units are canonical JSON (sorted keys, the same value rules, one object per key). digest(data, key=None) is sha256, or HMAC-SHA256 when a key is given. docs/formats/canonical-output.md documents it with one example per type

`golden record <eng> [--dataset engagement|seeds|all] [--private-only] [--check]` (toolkit/golden.py, commands/golden.py). Record the catalog units whose rules.json object has decision keep (Q in docs/contracts.md#pass-rate); units of dropped or out_of_scope objects get no manifest entry, so the harness never selects them. Load each dataset through ReferenceAdapter (engagement: {{p.private}}/reference/; seeds: {{p.private}}/synthetic/reference/), run every recorded unit whose catalog status is ok, canonicalise and write. Engagement goes to {{p.private}}/goldens/engagement/<file-safe id>.csv (or .json); seed-N goes to {{p.target}}/goldens/synthetic/seed-N/expected/<file-safe id>.csv (or .json). Use the file-safe id rule of `reference sql` (docs/contracts.md conventions: _ for each character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-], then - and the first 8 hex digits of sha256 when anything was replaced). Document goldens are JSON, never PDF or xlsx (the forbid-sample-outputs hook rejects those). `--dataset seeds` reads only committed seeds and the design zone, so it may run as `uv run toolkit golden record`; engagement and all run through mp-data, where the toolkit child may write only {{p.target}}/goldens/, the data zone and $TMPDIR (docs/contracts.md#data-plane-jail). If a reference database is missing, exit 2 and name the command that builds it (`uv run toolkit reference build <eng> --dataset seeds` or `mp-data reference build <eng> --dataset engagement`); a missing catalog names `uv run toolkit reference sql <eng> --all`. Under MP_QUIET=1 the summary carries `counts` per dataset and status and `units` [{id, status, reason, dataset}] for the units that are not ok, never values

Manifest {{p.target}}/goldens/manifest.json (docs/contracts.md#goldens-manifest): units keyed by id, each with area, kind, columns [{name, type}] from ReferenceAdapter.describe (null for documents), order_by ([{column, desc}] for the unit's ORDER BY on output columns, null when it has none), needs_access_confirmation (copied from the catalog) and canonical_version 1. datasets.engagement is {status, reason, rows, digest {alg: hmac-sha256, value}}; datasets.seed-N is {status, reason, rows, digest {alg: sha256, value}, expected: path relative to goldens/}. Status is ok, needs-params, unsupported, or empty (0 rows on that dataset). reason is null for ok, empty for empty, the catalog reason (action-query, crosstab, form-reference-unresolved, unsupported-function, pass-through, other) when the catalog status is not ok, and other when no workable parameter value was found on that dataset. rows and digest are set for ok and empty and null otherwise; a document unit's rows is its number of keys. The HMAC key is HMAC-SHA256(b"modpipe-golden-v1", bytes of the engagement data file), where the file is source.data_copy when set, else source.path. When that is a folder (vcs-export), the bytes of {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement/dataset.json are used instead (it lists every table's sha256). The key is computed in memory and never printed or written. Area and the keep decision come from the rules.json object that the catalog unit names; a unit whose object is missing from rules.json is recorded with area null, which `golden status` rejects. No values in the manifest

Parameters. The committed {{p.target}}/goldens/params.json holds each unit's definitions (name, type, source) and the seed values; engagement values go only to {{p.private}}/goldens/params.json. The tool picks values deterministically from each dataset. Key-like parameter: the smallest key that gives a non-empty result, at most 20 tries. Date parameter: the latest date in the filtered column. xlsm input cells: the shipped cell value for engagement; for seeds, a date input (dashboard as_of) takes the seed's latest invoice date and any other input takes the value a rule in {{p.records}}/answers.md gives. A choice rule stated in answers.md overrides this. A unit with no workable value gets needs-params with reason other

--check alone re-records into a temp dir and compares with the committed manifest, params and expected files (and with the private goldens when present). It exits 1 on any difference and writes nothing. --private-only records only the engagement dataset into {{p.private}}/goldens/ (outputs and engagement params) and never writes the target repo. Together, `--dataset engagement --private-only --check` writes {{p.private}}/goldens/ and then exits 1 when any engagement status, row count or digest differs from the committed manifest. The S2 exit criteria and the S5 and S6 prepare lists use that form to rebuild lost private state and prove it matches

`golden status {{p.target}}/goldens --rules {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json --dataset engagement --min-ok 0.9 --max-empty 0.25` (docs/contracts.md#pass-rate). Q = units whose rules.json object is kept. rate = units with status ok on the dataset / |Q|; empty share = units with status empty / |Q|. Exit 1 when the rate is below --min-ok, the empty share is above --max-empty, a unit's area is not a rules.json areas[].id, or a kept query (xlsm: a kept calculated column or formula block) has no unit. Print counts per status and per area, plus the ids that are not ok with their reasons (under MP_QUIET=1: `counts`, `rates.characterization` and `rates.empty_share`, and `units` [{id, status, reason, dataset}] for the units that are not ok). Read only committed files

Tests (toolkit/tests/test_golden.py and harness/tests/test_canonical.py, fixtures in toolkit/tests/fixtures/golden/): canonical formatting per type, ordering with and without order_by, NFC, HMAC versus sha256, file-safe ids, per-dataset status and reason, that --check catches a one-cell change, that --private-only refuses a digest mismatch, and status rates on a fixture manifest

The same wrapper sets MP_ONLY_AREAS from --eq-only-areas when that option is given, so the CI can limit areas without the toolkit; without the option it leaves an MP_ONLY_AREAS already in the environment unchanged. The plugin does not rely on app/conftest.py, which pytest does not load for ../equivalence/tests; the test database name comes from the settings module in adapter.toml (config.settings.test, S4.template)

`toolkit equivalence <eng> --adapter reference|django --datasets synthetic|engagement|all|<list> [--dbs postgresql|mssql|from-engagement] [-k EXPR] [--only-areas A[,B...]] [--collect-only] [--allow-not-implemented] [--allow-empty] [--min-pass-per-cell F] [--junit-dir DIR] [--matrix FILE]` (toolkit/equivalence.py, commands/equivalence.py). --datasets is required (no default): synthetic = every seed in the manifest, all = engagement plus the seeds, <list> = comma-separated names. Run one pytest process per (dataset, db) cell. --collect-only passes --collect-only to every cell, prints the test ids and runs nothing. --junit-dir DIR and --matrix FILE create missing parent directories. Every cell gets -k unchanged, --eq-only-areas for --only-areas (area ids must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,29}$, else exit 2) and --eq-allow-not-implemented for --allow-not-implemented. reference: run the vendored {{p.target}}/equivalence with the pipeline's Python (the toolkit's own interpreter, sys.executable, so no uv runs inside the jail), cwd {{p.target}}: `python -m pytest equivalence/tests -p equivalence.plugin --eq-adapter <temp adapter.toml> --eq-dataset <name> --eq-db reference --junitxml <file> -p no:cacheprovider`, where the temporary adapter.toml's entrypoint is toolkit.commands.reference:ReferenceAdapter. The db of each cell is `reference`; --adapter reference exits 2 when --dbs is given, and --adapter django exits 2 without it. django: use the exec line from docs/contracts.md#harness, read from {{p.target}}/equivalence/adapter.toml: `<python> -m pytest -c pyproject.toml --rootdir . ../equivalence/tests -p equivalence.plugin --create-db --eq-adapter ../equivalence/adapter.toml --eq-dataset <name> --eq-db <db> --junitxml <file> -p no:cacheprovider` with cwd app/. Inside mp-data (MP_SANDBOX is mp-data) <python> is the app's own interpreter <project_dir>/.venv/bin/python (app/.venv/bin/python), not the adapter.toml `python` command: the jail allows no uv, which would lock or sync the read-only app environment (docs/contracts.md#data-plane-jail). When that interpreter is missing, exit 2 naming `cd {{p.target}}/app && uv sync --locked`. Environment of every cell (both adapters): EQUIVALENCE_PRIVATE={{p.private}}; EQUIVALENCE_OBTAINED; EQUIVALENCE_REDACT=1 and EQUIVALENCE_DIGEST_KEY (computed as in S2.golden) for the engagement dataset; MP_DB_SUFFIX passed through. A django cell also gets: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE from settings; MP_ONLY_AREAS set to the --only-areas list when it is given (the overlay then installs only those areas' apps; mp-data passes --only-areas through, because a data-plane call carries no env prefix), and otherwise an MP_ONLY_AREAS already in the environment passed through unchanged (S5's per-item acceptance sets it as a command prefix); DATABASE_URL = server URL + '/{{e.db_name}}', where the server URL is MP_DATA_PG_URL or MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL when set (only inside mp-data, which gives equivalence the mp_runner URLs from data.env under both names, so data-plane runs connect as mp_runner, which owns the test databases it creates) and otherwise the variable named in databases[db] (PG_URL or MSSQL_URL); MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX passed through (mp-data sets mpdata_test_, so a data-plane run's test databases are mpdata_test_{{e.db_name}}_<slot>; unset means test_). A django cell on the engagement dataset exits 2 with 'run through mp-data' unless MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX is mpdata_test_ and the MP_DATA_ URL for its db is set. EQUIVALENCE_OBTAINED is {{p.private}}/synthetic/results/obtained/<dataset>-<db>/ when --junit-dir lies under {{p.private}}/synthetic/ and the run is not inside mp-data (synthetic-only runs), else a temp dir removed at exit: a data-plane run writes no design-zone file, because mp-data's toolkit child may write only the data zone, $TMPDIR and its declared outputs (docs/contracts.md#data-plane-jail). from-engagement = database.primary plus database.verify_also

Selection, rates and exit codes (docs/contracts.md#pass-rate). A cell where pytest selects nothing (pytest exit 5) is empty: it is reported as empty (total 0, rate null) and does not fail the run. Cell rate = passed / selected units, so with -k or --only-areas the denominator is the units the cell selected, and in a gate run (neither) it is |C_d|. Failed, error, skipped, xfail, xpass and not-implemented count as not passed. Exit 1 when a non-empty cell's rate is below --min-pass-per-cell F; without --min-pass-per-cell, when any selected test has an outcome other than passed or not-implemented; and, without --allow-not-implemented, when any not-implemented outcome occurs. --allow-not-implemented only stops not-implemented outcomes from failing the run; they still count as not passed. Exit 5 only when every cell is empty; with --allow-empty that case exits 0 with status no-data. Exit 2 on usage errors, a missing manifest, adapter.toml, dataset dir or environment variable, and when a cell's pytest exits with anything other than 0, 1 or 5. Without --junit-dir, JUnit and obtained files go to a temp dir that is removed at exit, so a run without --junit-dir and --matrix writes nothing outside {{p.private}}/logs/ (reviewers rely on this). --matrix writes counts only: format_version 1, cells [{dataset, db, status (ok or empty), passed, failed, errors, skipped, not_implemented, total, rate}]. stdout is the cell table, with empty cells marked, never values. build: toolkit/stage1.py builds SQLAlchemy MetaData from the design: --schema-from auto or model reads {{p.private}}/out/model/schema.json; data-model exits 2 'not built yet: S4.models adds it for workbooks'. It uses toolkit.typemap for every column. Original table and column names, quoted when needed; primary keys, unique indexes and literal defaults; foreign keys only for relationships with enforced integrity, keeping their cascade rules (on SQL Server a second cascade path to a table becomes NO ACTION). Everything not created is listed in the report. With --schema-only, stage1 reads only the design files (schema.json, or data-model.json once S4.models adds it) and the engagement, never the source, a dataset or any other data-zone path, so S4.models runs it with `uv run toolkit` outside mp-data

Dataset input through toolkit.dataset (contracts §7): --dataset engagement (the default) is {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement; --dataset DIR is any dataset directory, such as a synthetic seed's input/; --dataset fresh-copy is the back-end file at engagement database.stage1.fresh_copy (a data-zone path under {{p.private}}/sources/; cutover only), read with toolkit.dataset.open_backend after its tables, columns and types are checked against schema.json. Insert in foreign-key order in batches of 1000; keep autonumber values (SET IDENTITY_INSERT on SQL Server, GENERATED BY DEFAULT on PostgreSQL) and then move each identity or sequence past the maximum; omitted columns are listed, not loaded

--target-db takes three forms. `local:<name>`: database <name> on the local server of each dialect that --dialects selects (from-engagement = database.primary plus database.verify_also; required with local:). The server URL is MP_DATA_PG_URL or MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL when set, else PG_URL or MSSQL_URL; a dialect with neither exits 2 naming the variable. Inside mp-data, PG_URL and MSSQL_URL hold the superuser URLs from $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env (mp-data maps MP_DATA_PG_URL and MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL onto them, and leaves them unset when data.env lacks them); outside mp-data they are the mp_agent URLs of the env file. stage1 is a toolkit-only command (it runs no app code and no app-function rewrite), so mp-data gives it the superuser URLs, never the mp_runner ones (decisions L12.3). `secret:<ref>`: the client's server; resolves engagement secrets.<ref> (secret:stage1_target_url_ref) with toolkit.secrets.resolve; takes the dialect from the URL scheme, refuses --dialects and --replace, and never prints or logs the URL or any part of it. The jailed child cannot read data.env or the pass store (decisions L12.2), so mp-data resolves that ref before it starts the child and hands the value over only as MP_SECRET_SECRETS_STAGE1_TARGET_URL_REF, which toolkit.secrets.resolve reads under MP_SANDBOX=mp-data (S0.workspace, contracts §2). A literal URL (postgresql://... or mssql://..., one database on one server, dialect from the scheme, --dialects refused) is only for anchored non-mp-data commands such as S4.models' `--target-db "$PG_URL/{{e.db_name}}_dev"`; data-plane calls never carry one. URL mapping: postgresql:// becomes postgresql+psycopg and mssql:// becomes mssql+mssqlpython (TrustServerCertificate only for 127.0.0.1). purge (S6.report) reuses the local: server resolution and the URL mapping

Engagement rows only enter mpdata_ databases. With --dataset engagement, fresh-copy or a DIR under {{p.private}} (all engagement data) and without --schema-only, a local: name must start with mpdata_ and a literal URL is refused; both exit 2 'engagement data loads only into mpdata_* databases or a secret: target'. mp-data is stricter: it refuses a literal URL or a local: name without mpdata_ in every stage1 call. When a local: name starts with mpdata_ and the database already exists, stage1 reads its owner before it creates, loads or checks anything (PostgreSQL: pg_database.datdba; SQL Server: sys.databases.owner_sid) and exits 2 'mpdata_ database <name> is owned by <role>, not postgres, sa or mp_runner: drop it as the superuser' for any other owner, changing nothing. Reason: mp_agent has CREATEDB (CREATE ANY DATABASE on SQL Server), so it could create an mpdata_ database and own it; after the load it could read the rows as dbo on SQL Server, or rename the database past the pg_hba reject line on PostgreSQL. A database stage1 creates belongs to the superuser in its URL. The agent role in PG_URL (mp_agent) is rejected from mpdata_* databases by pg_hba, and on SQL Server mp_agent has no user in the databases sa creates, so only mp-data reaches the Stage 1 load. Agent databases ({{e.db_name}}_dev, {{e.db_name}}, test_{{e.db_name}}_<slot>) never hold engagement rows

Modes. Default (no --replace, no --verify): create the database if it is missing (local: and URL targets; never for secret:); when the target has no tables, create the schema and load; when the tables and row counts already match, do nothing; otherwise exit 1 'target differs; use --replace' (secret: targets: 'target not empty; ask the DBA to drop and recreate it'). --replace (local: and URL targets only; a secret: target must be an empty database the client provides): create the database if it is missing, drop every table in its default schema (public on PostgreSQL, dbo on SQL Server; foreign keys first), create the schema and load. --schema-only: DDL only, never rows and never a dataset; it combines with the default mode, --replace and --verify. --verify runs the checks: after the load when combined with --replace; without --replace it is read-only and never creates, loads or changes anything (a missing database or table is a failed check). Checks: tables, columns and mapped types (the SQL Server mp_rowversion column is ignored); primary keys, unique indexes and foreign keys; row counts; per-table sha256 over the sorted canonical rows (contracts §7 value rules) equal on both sides; no foreign-key orphans; identities past the maximum. With --schema-only the checks are tables, columns, mapped types, keys and foreign keys only. --require-rows: exit 1 when a target table has fewer rows than the dataset or every dataset table is empty

Output: honours MP_QUIET=1; stdout holds counts, names, sha256s of files and mismatch counts, never values; the summary (contracts §17) carries `tables`, one entry {table, dialect, dataset_rows, target_rows, digest_match, fk_orphans} per dialect and table, and no values. Under mp-data the child may write only into the data zone, $TMPDIR and the --report path (decisions L12.2), so stage1 writes nothing else. Exit 0 pass, 1 a check failed, 2 usage or missing input. --report FILE writes Markdown describing the verified state: one table per dialect (table, dataset rows, target rows, digest match yes or no, FK orphans), omitted columns, relationships not created, sha256 of schema.json and of the dataset. Per-table digests stay out of the report, and a secret: target is named by its dialect only. No timestamps, so --verify alone and --replace --verify on the same data give the same bytes: reviewers write theirs under {{p.private}}/review/<slot>/ (mp-data creates the directory) and compare it with cmp

toolkit/tests/test_stage1.py needs no database server. Hand-written fixtures in toolkit/tests/fixtures/stage1/: a 3-table schema.json with autonumber, yesno, currency, datetime, memo, a multi-value column and an enforced relationship, plus a matching dataset directory (dataset.json and tables/<table>.csv). Tests: DDL compiled for postgresql and mssql and compared with expected text; load, --verify and --require-rows on SQLite in memory; one changed cell gives a digest mismatch; an empty dataset fails --require-rows; a second run without --replace is a no-op; a differing target exits 1; --verify without --replace on an empty target fails and creates nothing; --schema-only with --replace and then with --verify while the dataset directory is absent (proves no dataset is read); --target-db parsing of local:, secret: and literal URLs, with --dialects required for local: and refused for the other two; local: server URLs taken from MP_DATA_* before PG_URL or MSSQL_URL, and exit 2 naming a missing one; engagement data (engagement, fresh-copy or a DIR under the private directory) into a local: name without the mpdata_ prefix or into a literal URL exits 2; --replace on a secret: target exits 2; the create-if-missing statements for both dialects, recorded by a fake engine; an existing mpdata_ database owned by mp_agent (fake engine) exits 2 and changes nothing, while owners postgres, sa and mp_runner pass; the summary's tables entries validate against toolkit/schemas/summary.schema.json; URL mapping; under MP_SANDBOX=mp-data a secret: target resolves from MP_SECRET_SECRETS_STAGE1_TARGET_URL_REF without opening data.env, and its URL never appears in output, logs or the report. A fresh-copy case starts a JVM like S2's toolkit/tests/test_bridge_sources.py (JAVA_HOME and the vendor/ jars, which a demo's `mp-data fetch` and a client's S0 prepare jar fetch put in this worktree) and still needs no database server: it creates an .accdb in tmp_path from the fixture dataset through toolkit.reference.bridge, as that test does, without the multi-value column (Jackcess 5.1.7 cannot create complex columns; the schema.json the case uses leaves it out too), points a test engagement's database.stage1.fresh_copy at it, loads it with `--dataset fresh-copy` into a local mpdata_ test database (`--target-db local:mpdata_stage1_test --dialects from-engagement`, the local server's engine patched to SQLite in memory) and checks that every table's row count equals the fixture's

templates/docs/stage1-runbook.md (headings: Before you start, ODBC driver and Office bitness, Connection string, Relink the tables, Front-end changes, Backups and restore, Rollback) and templates/docs/stage1-cutover.md (headings: Freeze window, Fresh copy, Load and verify, Relink, Smoke checklist, Rollback, Sign-off) are skeletons. Fill the engagement copies in {{p.target}}/docs/ from the engagement (database, database.stage1, secret references by name only), stage1-frontend-changes.md and, when it exists, the rules.json workflows. The runbook covers ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server or psqlODBC ('True is -1', 'Row Versioning') matching Office bitness, relinking every table, each front-end change, pg_dump or SQL Server backups and their restore, and rollback by relinking to the old back end. The cutover's Load and verify section holds two exact commands, the load `mp-data stage1 {{p.records}}/engagement.json --target-db secret:stage1_target_url_ref --dataset fresh-copy` and then the check `mp-data stage1 {{p.records}}/engagement.json --target-db secret:stage1_target_url_ref --dataset fresh-copy --verify --require-rows --report {{p.records}}/stage1-cutover-report.md`, and says: run them in a plain terminal on the operator host, outside any Claude session; if the load stops part-way, have the DBA drop and recreate the empty database, then run both commands again

Discovery: config/discovery.py discover_local_apps(APPS_DIR) returns sorted '<slug>.<name>' for every APPS_DIR/*/apps.py except users. When the environment variable MP_ONLY_AREAS is set and not empty (comma-separated area ids), it returns only core, legacy and domain (those that exist) plus the named areas, chosen by directory name without importing any other area's apps.py, and raises ImproperlyConfigured naming any id that has no package; core's autodiscover_modules('saved_queries') covers installed apps only, so a half-written area cannot break another item's run. Unset or empty means every area. core/local/roles.py: ROLES maps each role name to its label, its permissions and the rule ids it comes from, mirroring the source app's privileges in rules.json. `manage.py import_dataset DIR [--flush]`: loads a dataset directory (docs/contracts.md#dataset-directory: goldens/synthetic/seed-N/input or {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement) through legacy/resources.py, and through legacy/import_map.py when it exists; prints per-table counts only; row errors name the table, row number and column, never a value. import_dataset: read dataset.json and tables/*.csv with the vendored reader (equivalence/dataset.py; the target root is on sys.path through manage.py and pytest's pythonpath); load tables in dataset.json load_order; map each table through legacy/import_map.py IMPORT_MAP when the table is in it, else to the model whose db_table equals the table name, using legacy/resources.py RESOURCES (validation, foreign-key resolution, history rows with change reason 'import <dataset name>'); keep primary-key values, then reset sequences (PostgreSQL: connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql; SQL Server: IDENTITY_INSERT during the load and DBCC CHECKIDENT afterwards); --flush deletes legacy rows in reverse load order first; per-table counts only on stdout. Before loading, the loader checks the target: dataset.json kind engagement on a database whose host is 127.0.0.1 or localhost is refused with CommandError (returncode 2), naming the database but no value, when its NAME does not start with mpdata_ or when its owner (PostgreSQL: pg_database.datdba; SQL Server: sys.databases.owner_sid) is not postgres, sa or mp_runner, the rule stage1 applies (mp_agent may create databases, so it could own an mpdata_ one). A data-plane equivalence run passes, because Django creates its test database through mp-data's runner URL, so mp_runner owns it

equivalence.py: DjangoAdapter(load_dataset(dir), run_saved_query(unit_id, params) -> rows in the manifest's column order, render_document(unit_id, key, params) -> the canonical fields of docs/contracts.md#documents). Unregistered units raise equivalence.adapter.NotImplementedUnit (it subclasses NotImplementedError; the JUnit outcome is skipped with type equivalence.not-implemented). It reads only the database, never golden files, never branches on dataset identity and writes no files: under mp-data the app runs on app/.venv/bin/python (the jail has no uv) with everything read-only except this engagement's data zone, $TMPDIR and the run's declared outputs

vbacompat.py: the Access and VBA functions the kept queries and reports call (from objects.json), at least Format (named formats General Date, Long Date, Medium Date, Short Date, Long Time, Short Time, Currency, Fixed, Standard, Percent, Yes/No, True/False, On/Off, plus the custom date and number characters in use), Nz, IIf, DateValue, DateSerial, DateAdd, DateDiff, DatePart, Year, Month, Day, Weekday, Left, Right, Mid, Len, InStr, Trim, UCase, LCase, CStr, CInt, CLng, CDbl, CCur, Int, Fix and Round (banker's rounding, as VBA does). Port behaviour from Jackcess's expression Format code (impl/expr in spannm/jackcess 5.1.7, Apache-2.0) in your own structure, and credit it in core/THIRD_PARTY.md with the Apache-2.0 notice. Table-driven tests; each expected value cites Microsoft's documentation or a Jackcess test. Excel worksheet functions (WORKDAY, SUMIFS) belong to S5.shared's domain/, not here

testing.py is a pytest plugin module (app/conftest.py loads it); load_seed resolves seeds from settings.BASE_DIR.parent / 'goldens/synthetic'; user_with_role uses the role groups and allauth EmailAddress
reuse: django-import-export Resource.import_data with dry_run=False and use_transactions=True
django.core.management.color.no_style() with connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql

tasks.title: Review the foundation
lenses: Foundation, portability and reuse: a Django developer who knows cookiecutter-django recognises everything; templates/django-overlay holds nothing engagement-specific (engagement code only in core/local/); production settings are safe (DEBUG off, hosts, secret key and email from env, registration closed, Microsoft sign-in off unless configured); later apps register by discovery with no edit to config/, and MP_ONLY_AREAS limits discovery to the named areas plus users, core, legacy and domain; concurrent runs get separate test databases (<MP_TEST_DB_PREFIX><db_name>_<slot>, cut and hashed above 63 characters); a DATABASE_URL in the environment wins over app/.env, with $PG_URL/<db_name> as the fallback; PostgreSQL and SQL Server both pass (sites migration guard, python_driver mssql_python); target CI uses no toolkit, secrets or engagement data, and its e2e steps run only when tests/e2e has test_*.py and write no screenshots or video; the root pre-commit config keeps every S0 hook unchanged; new-app --check covers only manifest files and never writes

Model and data fidelity: every kept table, column, key and index from rules.json and the design (data-model.json for xlsm) is a managed model that keeps db_table and db_column; on_delete and choices match rules.json relations and lookups; each data-macro validation is a clean() or constraint with a test naming its rule id; migrations are fresh (kept tables in 0001, history in 0002); {{e.db_name}}_dev is schema-only, the app dev database {{e.db_name}} and agent test databases hold synthetic data only, no task read client rows, and import_dataset meets the engagement dataset only inside mp-data (it refuses a local database without the mpdata_ prefix or owned by a role other than postgres, sa or mp_runner); import_dataset loads seed-1 with counts equal to dataset.json and prints no values; the adapter reports not implemented instead of guessing and writes no files; vbacompat cases are documented and credit Jackcess; for xlsm, import_map.py turns the repeated line columns into invoice lines and the customer columns into a foreign key

gate.name: Runs on test data
client: Check the integrate report: every exit criterion passed. The `mp-data equivalence ... --min-pass-per-cell 0.9` line (the report shows it as `mp-data --slot <slot> equivalence ...`) means the lowest dataset × database cell (the client's data and seeds 1 to 3, on every database in database.primary and database.verify_also) is at least 0.90; the app test runs mean rule tests and e2e pass 100%. In a plain terminal (the client session denies results/), open the per-cell counts in {{p.private}}/results/S5/matrix.json and share them with the client; they hold counts, never values

Before the session the client or their MSP provides a staging host and an empty staging database (engagement hosting and database.primary) and lets the operator host reach that database for the load. Its URL reaches the operator host only as the secret that secrets.staging_db_url_ref names (`pass:<path>`, or `env:NAME` in $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env). Nobody pastes the URL into a prompt, a repo file or chat

Rehearse the load on the operator host first, in a plain terminal outside Claude, with only the env file sourced (`. {{p.env_file}}`). Engagement rows go only into mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate, which mp_agent and every agent session are refused. The app is agent-written code, so it gets the runner role mp_runner and nothing else from data.env: never source $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env into this shell (the app would see every secret in it) and never give the app MP_DATA_PG_URL or MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL. That keeps the other secrets out of the app's environment, not out of its reach: the app runs as you, outside mp-run and the mp-data jail, so app code that tried could still open data.env or the pass store. This is a recorded residual risk (proposal §11, hostile-agent residuals): the isolation stops accidental exposure by agents that follow their prompts, and the S5.review equivalence-integrity lens is what checks the app code first. Run `docker exec mp-pg16 dropdb -U postgres --if-exists mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate` and `docker exec mp-pg16 createdb -U postgres -O mp_runner mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate`, then in {{p.target}}/app `export DATABASE_URL="$(. $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && printf %s "$MP_RUNNER_PG_URL")/mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate"`, `uv run python manage.py migrate` and `uv run python manage.py import_dataset {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement`. It prints per-table counts only; they must equal the rows in {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement/dataset.json. When database.primary is mssql, create the database with `(. $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && SQLCMDPASSWORD=$MP_MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD docker exec -e SQLCMDPASSWORD mp-mssql22 /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -C -S localhost -U sa -b -Q 'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate; CREATE DATABASE mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate; ALTER AUTHORIZATION ON DATABASE::mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate TO mp_runner')` and take MP_RUNNER_MSSQL_URL instead of MP_RUNNER_PG_URL. When the counts match, run `unset DATABASE_URL` and drop the database the same way (`docker exec mp-pg16 dropdb -U postgres mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate`, or `DROP DATABASE mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate` through sqlcmd); `mp-data purge` drops it too if it is left over. A failure is a defect: re-run S5 with args.rerun and args.since before staging is touched

Deploy the S5 commit to staging following {{p.target}}/docs/staging.md, with settings from the host's environment variables and DATABASE_URL from secrets.staging_db_url_ref, then run `python manage.py migrate` there

Load the client's test data into the staging database yourself, in a plain terminal on the operator host (outside Claude; the client session blocks it): in {{p.target}}/app, with only the env file sourced and DATABASE_URL taken from the secret that secrets.staging_db_url_ref names, never echoed (`env:NAME`: `export DATABASE_URL="$(. $HOME/.config/modernization/data.env && printf %s "$NAME")"`; `pass:<path>`: `export DATABASE_URL="$(pass show <path> | head -n 1)"`), run `uv run python manage.py import_dataset {{p.private}}/datasets/engagement`, then `unset DATABASE_URL`. It prints per-table counts only. As in the rehearsal, the app runs outside any jail here (the same residual risk, proposal §11). Engagement rows go only to the client's staging server and to mpdata_ databases, never to {{e.db_name}}, {{e.db_name}}_dev or a test_ database
Create one staging account per tester with the right role (Django admin, or the Entra group mapping when engagement auth uses Entra) and send them the sign-in link

The client's staff run every must_keep workflow and every kept report on staging with their test data, following analysis/rules.md. Sort each finding: a defect (re-run S5 with args.rerun ["S5.feature.<area id>"] or ["S5.shared"] and args.since describing the defect without data values), an answer to an open question ({{p.records}}/answers.md, rules only, never data), or new behaviour (a change order through S1.change_order, priced before any work)
When the client accepts and the target CI checks pass, record {{p.records}}/gates.json S5 {approved}, squash-merge the S5 PRs and invoice the 40% milestone (engagement commercial.milestones)
Record your gate and review minutes in {{p.records}}/log.md
demo: Check the integrate report: every exit criterion passed, including the `mp-data equivalence ... --min-pass-per-cell 0.9` line (shown as `mp-data --slot <slot> equivalence ...`; engagement data and seeds 1 to 3 on PostgreSQL and SQL Server, lowest cell at least 0.90) and the app test runs on both databases. In a plain terminal, read the per-cell counts in {{p.private}}/results/S5/matrix.json (counts only) and note the lowest cell for the equivalence report

Click through the app on seed 1 in your own terminal, with the env file sourced (`. {{p.env_file}}`). Run `{{p.pipeline}}/scripts/dev_db.sh dropdb {{e.db_name}}` and `{{p.pipeline}}/scripts/dev_db.sh createdb {{e.db_name}}` (as mp_agent; {{e.db_name}} holds synthetic data only; engagement rows never go there). Then in {{p.target}}/app, with DEMO_PASSWORD set in your shell to a password you choose, run `uv run python manage.py migrate`, `uv run python manage.py import_dataset ../goldens/synthetic/seed-1/input`, `uv run python manage.py create_demo_users` and `uv run python manage.py runserver`

Follow every must_keep workflow as a user would. Northwind: sign in, order → invoice PDF → ship; purchase order → receive → stock level. InvoiceGenerator: add customer → create invoice → PDF, xlsx and .eml → mark paid → dashboard for an as-of date. Write anything confusing in log.md; a real defect means a re-run with args.rerun ["S5.feature.<area id>"] and args.since describing it
Look through {{p.target}}/docs/img/after/: each workflow and each kept area's main screen, seed-1 data only, readable at 1280x800. These pictures go into the README and the equivalence report at S6
Watch {{p.private}}/synthetic/media/walkthrough/walkthrough.webm once (seed-1 data). It is narrated and uploaded at the S6 gate, not now

Wait for the target CI checks on the PR (lint, tests on PostgreSQL and SQL Server, harness on seeds 1 to 3, e2e on seed 1), then record {{p.records}}/gates.json S5 {approved} and the log row, and squash-merge the S5 PRs (pipeline docs/runbook.md 2(i) steps 6 and 7)

Log hours: record your gate, review and other minutes in the S5 row of {{p.records}}/log.md, add up the engagement's minutes so far and compare them with commercial.budget_hours in engagement.json. At 75% or more, say so in the row

Shared means a function or calculation that rules (rules[].sources), services or saved-query designs of two or more kept areas use. Find them in {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json, the query designs in {{p.private}}/out/model/ and the rewrites in {{p.target}}/goldens/reference/functions/. Data macros with side effects (After Insert, After Update, After Delete) that S4.models listed in its notes: when two or more kept areas write the table, implement the side effect here as a domain function that those areas' services call, citing the macro's rule id, with a test. A side effect on a table that only one area writes belongs to that area (S5.features)

Each function comes in the forms the areas need: an expression helper for querysets (for example with_product_on_order(queryset), adding an annotation built from Subquery, Coalesce and Case that works in filter() and order_by()) and a plain function for one object. Where both exist, a test shows they agree. ORM only, portable to PostgreSQL and SQL Server; nulls and rounding as the original handles them (vbacompat for Nz and Format; currency to 4 places as in docs/contracts.md#canonical-output)

Working days as Excel WORKDAY with no holiday list: step forward one day at a time and count only Monday to Friday; the start date is never counted. The database form is a Case on ExtractIsoWeekDay and must agree with the Python form for a start date on each day of the week

tasks.title: Build each feature area
tasks.scout: Read only {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json. Return one item per area whose status is kept, in the file's order: id exactly the area id, title exactly the area title, and scope one string 'queries: <names of the area's kept query objects>; rules: <the area's rule ids>' with ', ' between names. Use exactly the kept area ids in rules.json; never invent, rename, merge or split an area. Put in uncovered every kept object whose area is not a kept area id. If more than 4 areas are kept, still return all of them; the driver blocks the run and the orchestrator decides.

items_from.jq: . as $r | [.areas[] | select(.status=="kept") | {id, title, scope: (.id as $a | ["queries: " + ([$r.objects[] | select(.type=="query" and .area==$a and .decision=="keep") | .name] | join(", ")), "rules: " + ([$r.rules[] | select(.area==$a) | .id] | join(", "))] | join("; "))}]

reuse: templates/feature-app/ (S5.shared): copy it and replace the tokens as its README says
domain/ functions (S5.shared) for every shared calculation; never re-implement one
core (S4.data): the saved-query registry, the roles, the testing fixtures load_seed and user_with_role; vbacompat for VBA functions
legacy models, admin and factories (S4.models)

django-tables2 and django-filter for lists, django-crispy-forms with crispy-bootstrap5 for forms, django-htmx with django-template-partials for partial updates, django-weasyprint for PDFs, openpyxl (installed with django-import-export[xlsx]) for Excel, django.core.mail.EmailMessage for .eml files

{{p.target}}/app/{{e.app.slug}}/legacy/ (S4.models: models, admin, resources, factories) and {{p.target}}/app/{{e.app.slug}}/core/ (S4.data: registries, roles, testing fixtures, vbacompat.py); read-only

each.goal: Build the {{item.title}} area as the Django app {{e.app.slug}}.{{item.id}} following docs/contracts.md#feature-app-contract: its saved queries, services, screens, reports and documents, with one test per rule. Scope: {{item.scope}}. Every result comes from the database through the ORM and the domain functions; never read golden files and never branch on dataset, seed or row ids. Other areas are built at the same time in the same tree. Your acceptance and verify commands start Django with MP_ONLY_AREAS={{item.id}} (the mp-data line passes --only-areas {{item.id}}), so Django loads only your area plus users, core, legacy and domain; run your own Django commands (pytest, manage.py, toolkit equivalence --adapter django) the same way. The mp-data line runs your code in a jail that keeps both repos and the design zone read-only: build downloads in memory, use only the temp directory (Python's tempfile, which follows TMPDIR) for scratch files, and write no file anywhere else. The stage exit criteria load every area together, so keep your modules importable at every step (apps.py last, as the skeleton README says) and never edit another area, config/, core/, legacy/, domain/, users/ or templates/base.html (use requests).
deliverables: app/{{e.app.slug}}/{{item.id}}/ copied from {{p.pipeline}}/templates/feature-app/ with the tokens replaced: apps.py (name '{{e.app.slug}}.{{item.id}}', label '{{item.id}}', feature = True, nav_label '{{item.title}}') and urls.py (app_name '{{item.id}}'). The overlay mounts it at /{{item.id}}/ and adds it to the nav. No models or migrations in the area: the tables are legacy/ (S4.models); ask for a missing field with a request

saved_queries.py: every unit in {{p.target}}/goldens/manifest.json whose area is {{item.id}} and whose kind is saved_query or formula_output, registered with @saved_query('<unit id>'), taking the unit's params (definitions in goldens/params.json) and returning rows with the manifest's columns in order. ORM first; raw SQL only when the ORM cannot express it, and then portable to PostgreSQL and SQL Server

tasks.title: Review features
lenses: Equivalence integrity. Read every feature app under {{p.target}}/app/{{e.app.slug}}/, domain/ and their tests. Blocking: a hard-coded result, row list or expected value in app code; a branch on dataset name, seed number, row id or database vendor that changes results; app code that opens goldens/, equivalence/, manifest.json, params.json or any path under {{p.private}}, or writes a file outside the temp directory (mp-data's jail keeps both repos read-only); a @saved_query or @document id that is not a manifest unit of the same area, or a kept manifest unit of the area that nothing registers; a saved query or service that re-implements a domain/ function; raw SQL that only one database accepts; a skipped, xfailed, deleted or weakened test, or rounding looser than docs/contracts.md#canonical-output; -k, --only-areas, --allow-empty or any other deselection in an exit criterion; a rule test whose assertion does not check its rule's statement. Run S5.shared's verify list and each S5.feature item's verify list: its mp-data equivalence line covers the engagement data and seeds 1 to 3 on every database, and a cell below 0.90 or a not-implemented unit is a blocking issue against that item (a cell the summary reports as empty, because the area has no unit with status ok on that dataset, is not a failure). Per-item lines load one area (MP_ONLY_AREAS or --only-areas); the exit criteria load every area. Also blocking: a vendored file whose sha256 is not in its area's THIRD_PARTY.md, a Chart.js other than stack.app_assets.chartjs (4.5.1), or a CDN link. Never open the data zone; the mp-data summary is your only view of engagement results

Workflow completeness and usability. Must keep: {{e.scope.must_keep}}. For every workflow in {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json, an e2e test follows all its steps and asserts what the user sees, and {{p.target}}/docs/img/after/ shows it (1280x800, at most 400 KB, seed-1 data only, no error page or cut-off form). Every kept form and report in keep-drop.md has a screen or print view in the area its target_component names. Every rule with test_kind rule has a test in its area's tests/test_rules.py that checks the rule's statement, not a placeholder. Screens are usable by the client's staff: lists search and filter, forms show plain validation messages that name the field and the rule, PDF reports fit A4 and carry the fields of the original report design in {{p.private}}/out/model/, the nav lists every area, and a user without an area's role is refused. Workbooks: the PDF, xlsx and .eml downloads carry the fields of docs/contracts.md#documents, and the dashboard KPIs follow the as-of date. Run S5.e2e's verify list; it writes screenshots and the walkthrough video only under {{p.private}}/synthetic/media/<your slot>/ (seed-1 data, design zone), and you may open them to judge the screens

stages.offer_note: final 30% milestone: acceptance; the care plan starts if purchased

gate.name: Accepted
client: Send the client docs/equivalence-report.md and go through it with them: the lowest cell rate (the gate is at least 0.90 in every dataset and database cell), rule and end-to-end tests at 100%, and every known difference with its reason. Record their written acceptance in {{p.records}}/gates.json as S6 {"approved": "YYYY-MM-DD"}, then squash-merge the S6 PRs

Deploy to the client's host with docs/deploy/ and docs/runbook.md (engagement hosting.provider; hosting.managed_by says who runs it). The client or their MSP enters production settings and secrets in the host from the names the runbook lists; nobody pastes a value into a prompt, file or chat. Go live as the runbook's Go-live and smoke checklist section says, then create the first admin user and run the smoke checklist with a client user. hosting.managed_by us needs care_plan.purchased true; otherwise hand the hosting to the client at this gate.

Backups: turn on the host's automated database backups as the runbook's 'Backups and restore drill' section says. Run the restore drill once with the client or MSP: restore the latest backup into a scratch database, point a staging copy at it, run the smoke checklist, and record the date and result in {{p.records}}/log.md

Microsoft sign-in (engagement auth.mode microsoft-entra): the client's admin adds the redirect URIs from the runbook to the app registration and stores the client secret under the reference in secrets.entra.client_secret_ref. For every auth.mode, add {date, what} entries to care_plan.calendar in {{p.records}}/engagement.json: secrets.entra.secret_expires (microsoft-entra only), secrets.github_push.expires when the token is kept, the next quarterly restore drill when the care plan includes it, and the Django 5.2 end of support (2028-04)

Transfer access with docs/access-and-ownership.md: the client owns the GitHub repo, the host, the database and the app registration. Remove our access that the care plan does not need, revoke the push token in secrets.github_push unless the care plan needs it, and set care_plan.access_after_acceptance in engagement.json; when it differs from the After acceptance section of docs/access-and-ownership.md, correct that section in a follow-up target PR

Data retention: the end date is the acceptance date plus data_policy.retention_days_after_acceptance, unless care_plan.private_data says to keep it encrypted for the care plan. In a plain terminal (mp-data reads the database superuser URLs from data.env) run `mp-data purge {{p.records}}/engagement.json --dry-run` now and check it lists what docs/data-retention.md says: the private directory, the engagement's databases on every running local server (mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_*, mpdata_test_{{e.db_name}}_*, {{e.db_name}}_dev, {{e.db_name}} and test_{{e.db_name}}_*) and the Windows-box copies in environment.windows_box.copies. On the end date run it without --dry-run, delete the Windows-box copies it lists, commit {{p.records}}/destruction-record-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md in the records repo with rgit (runbook section 7) and send the client a copy

Invoice the final 30% (the S6 gate milestone in commercial.milestones). If care_plan.purchased is true, the care plan starts on the acceptance date with the monthly fee and included hours in the engagement's care_plan

Compare the engagement's total hours in {{p.records}}/log.md with commercial.budget_hours and with hours.point in {{p.records}}/estimate.json; write both ratios and the effective rate (invoiced USD / hours) in the S6 row (pipeline docs/runbook.md section 3, Recalibration)
Record your gate and review minutes in {{p.records}}/log.md
demo: Read docs/equivalence-report.md as a buyer would: the lowest of the cells (engagement, seed-1, seed-2 and seed-3 on PostgreSQL and SQL Server) is at least 0.90, rule and end-to-end tests are at 100%, every known difference has a reason, and the SQL Server cells say they come from the local Docker run

Read the {{e.id}} section of the root README, the app README, docs/runbook.md and NOTICE.md. Every number matches equivalence/results.json; before pictures say they are reconstructed and after pictures (docs/img/after/<workflow id>-<NN>-<step>.png and <area id>-main.png) show synthetic seed-1 data only

Legal check with docs/legal-check.md: every published path is own work, derived from names and structure only (no data, VBA, query or macro text), third-party licensed and credited in NOTICE.md, or synthetic. LICENSE is MIT for our code only
Squash-merge the S6 PRs

Record the walkthrough from the merged main in a plain terminal: `git -C {{p.target_repo}} switch main && git -C {{p.target_repo}} pull --ff-only`, then `. {{p.env_file}} && export MP_DB_SUFFIX=s6_gate && cd {{p.target}}/app && E2E_VIDEO_DIR={{p.private}}/synthetic/media/walkthrough uv run pytest -q --create-db -m walkthrough tests/e2e` writes {{p.private}}/synthetic/media/walkthrough/walkthrough.webm (seed-1 data only; never committed). Narrate it with docs/walkthrough.md and upload it unlisted

Pre-flip checks in {{p.target_repo}} on the merged main, with the commands of section 6 of the orchestrator runbook (pipeline docs/runbook.md, steps 3 to 9); all must pass: `git fetch --all --prune --tags`; delete every remote stage branch whose PR was merged (`gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged` lists it) with `git push origin --delete <branch>`; `git branch -r --no-merged origin/main` prints nothing; the plain data-plane call `mp-data guard {{p.records}}/engagement.json --repo {{p.pipeline}} --repo {{p.target_repo}} --history` passes; no forbidden file name was ever committed (`git log --all --name-only --format= | sort -u | grep -Ei '[.](accdt|accdb|accde|mdb|mde|laccdb|ldb|mdw|xlsm|xlsb|xls|xlam|bas|cls|frm|frx|msg|bak|pdf|eml|xlsx)$|^(private|data|vendor)/'` prints nothing); Actions logs and artifacts become public too, so delete every GitHub Actions run from the private period (`gh run list --limit 1000`, then `gh run delete <id>` for each); read every PR title, body and comment (`gh pr list --state all --limit 200 --json number,title,body,comments`) and fix any that mention client material, private paths or internal notes

On a branch {{e.id}}/S6-publish in the target repo: fill the Pre-flip checks table (date, main commit, result per check) and the Decision section of docs/legal-check.md, and replace the video line in the {{e.id}} section of the root README with the unlisted link. Before you push the branch, run the guard with --history again (the repo may already be public).
