build: toolkit/results.py and commands/results.py (cli.py discovers it): `toolkit results summarize <eng> --junit-dir DIR [--junit-dir DIR ...] --out FILE`, run only as `mp-data results summarize` because it reads {{p.private}}/results/ (data zone). The required cells come from the engagement and the committed manifest, never from a file in the JUnit directories: equivalence cells for `engagement` plus every seed-N dataset in {{p.target}}/goldens/manifest.json, on every database in database.primary and database.verify_also; app files junit-app-fixtures-postgresql.xml and, when mssql is among those databases, junit-app-fixtures-mssql.xml. It reads the files named junit-<suite>-<dataset>-<db>.xml for those cells from the --junit-dir directories (not recursively) with xml.etree: suite `equivalence` (one file per cell) or `app` (dataset `fixtures`). A required file found in no directory exits 1 naming it; a file found in two directories, or malformed XML, exits 2; files for other cells are ignored and named in the summary messages. Each app file is split into `rules` (test cases from */tests/test_rules.py, dataset fixtures) and `e2e` (test cases under tests/e2e/, dataset seed-1); other app tests count in neither. A split with no test cases gives no cell, so the SQL Server app file (run without tests/e2e) gives a rules cell only. Per cell it counts passed, failed, errors, skipped (pytest records xfail as skipped), not_implemented (skipped with type equivalence.not-implemented) and total (test cases); rate = passed / total, 0 when total is 0. Inside mp-data's jail (contracts data-plane-jail) its only declared output is --out. Honours MP_QUIET=1; the summary (contracts summary-schema) carries counts, rates min_cell and pooled over the equivalence cells, and cells with the results.json cell fields without not_passed; never a failure message

results.json (sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline, no wall-clock time) in the contracts harness shape: format_version 1, engagement, date (the latest testsuite timestamp in the inputs, YYYY-MM-DD), cells [{suite, dataset, db, passed, failed, errors, skipped, not_implemented, total, rate}]. Two additions the report needs: every equivalence cell has not_passed [{unit, outcome}] (unit ids as in goldens/manifest.json; outcome failed, error, skipped or not_implemented), and a top-level gate {min_cell_rate, pooled_rate, threshold 0.9} over the equivalence cells. Counts and unit ids only: failure messages, system-out, system-err and properties are never copied

toolkit/report.py and commands/report.py: `toolkit report <eng> --results FILE --out FILE [--check]` loads the engagement with toolkit.engagement.load and reads results.json, {{p.target}}/goldens/manifest.json, {{p.target}}/analysis/rules.json, {{p.target}}/docs/known-differences.json, {{p.private}}/out/inventory.json, the file names in {{p.target}}/docs/img/after/ and the rule ids in docstrings of {{p.target}}/app/<slug>/*/tests/test_rules.py. It reads only committed files and the design-zone inventory: never the data zone and never the reference catalog. It renders templates/docs/equivalence-report.md with string.Template into the 8 sections in this order: Summary (the gate figure = lowest cell rate against 0.90, then the pooled rate and the coverage-adjusted rate (passed over |Q| times the number of cells, |Q| from the manifest), rule and e2e results); Method (reference engine for the source kind, engagement dataset plus synthetic seeds 1-3, the databases, canonical form version, HMAC digests for engagement outputs, redacted failure output); Results by dataset and database (one row per cell: passed, total, rate); Results by output kind (saved_query, formula_output, document); Coverage (kept units, characterization rate and empty share on engagement data, kept rules with a test, objects kept, dropped and out of scope from rules.json, inventory counts, and for Access kinds the fixed report-coverage sentence of build[8]); Rule tests and end-to-end tests (counts, and each workflow's after screenshots in docs/img/after/ as links); Known differences (every not-passed unit and cell with its reason from known-differences.json, plus every kept unit not characterized on a dataset, with that dataset's status and reason from goldens/manifest.json, such as action-query or crosstab); How to re-run (the vendored harness on synthetic seeds from equivalence/README.md; the engagement dataset runs only on our side through mp-data). Before rendering it checks every equivalence cell's total against |C_d| from the manifest (kept units with status ok on that dataset; contracts pass-rate)

SQL Server wording: the report names a database only when results.json has its cells, says SQL Server cells come from local runs in Docker (mp-mssql22), and calls target-repo CI a cross-check on synthetic seeds. It never reads CI artifacts and never claims 'both databases' without both sets of cells

report exits 1 and lists the reasons when the lowest cell rate is below 0.90, an equivalence cell's total differs from |C_d|, rule or e2e tests are below 100% or results.json has no rules cell or no e2e cell, the characterization rate is below 0.90 or empty outputs are above 25% on engagement data, a kept rule has no test, or a not-passed unit and cell has no known-differences entry; it still writes --out so the gap is visible. --check renders in memory, compares with --out byte for byte, exits 1 on any difference and writes nothing. No timestamps other than results.json's date, so two runs give the same bytes

known-differences.json (written by you for this engagement): {format_version 1, entries [{unit, cells ['<dataset>:<db>'], reason, rule_ids}]}. Find reasons on synthetic seeds with `uv run toolkit equivalence {{p.records}}/engagement.json --adapter django --datasets synthetic --dbs from-engagement -k '::<unit id>::'`; for a unit that fails only on engagement data, use only the counts and column names in the mp-data summary and say so in the reason. Never quote values

toolkit/purge.py and commands/purge.py: `toolkit purge <eng> [--dry-run]`, run only as `mp-data purge`. It is a toolkit-only command, so mp-data gives it the superuser URLs, never the mp_runner ones (contracts databases and mp-data). It finds each local server with toolkit.stage1's local: server resolution and URL mapping (S3.move: MP_DATA_PG_URL or MP_DATA_MSSQL_URL when set, else PG_URL or MSSQL_URL; inside mp-data both names hold the same superuser URL). Inside mp-data's jail (contracts data-plane-jail) its declared outputs are {{p.private}} and {{p.records}}, and every other engagement's record/ and private/ are masked, so mp-data passes their db_names in MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES (comma-separated, built before the jail starts from every other engagement.json under $HOME/engagements/*/record/ and {{p.pipeline}}/engagements/: db_name, or the id with every character outside [a-z0-9] replaced by _). purge exits 2 when MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES is unset; an empty value means no other engagement. It deletes everything under {{p.private}}, then the directory itself; a directory that is a mount point, as {{p.private}} is in the jail, is emptied and stays. The call's own TMPDIR and mp-data log lie under {{p.private}}/logs/ and go with the rest (mp-data expects that), so purge needs no temporary file once it starts deleting. On every running local dialect (PostgreSQL, and SQL Server when its container answers) it lists the databases (pg_database without templates; sys.databases) and drops every one named mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_* (the Stage 1 load mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_stage1, the gate import mpdata_{{e.db_name}}_gate), mpdata_test_{{e.db_name}}_*, {{e.db_name}}_dev, {{e.db_name}} or test_{{e.db_name}}_*. It matches names in Python with exact prefixes, never with SQL LIKE (where _ is a wildcard), and drops in autocommit: `DROP DATABASE "<name>" WITH (FORCE)` on PostgreSQL; `ALTER DATABASE [<name>] SET SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE`, then `DROP DATABASE [<name>]` on SQL Server. A name that also matches these patterns for another engagement whose db_name begins with this db_name plus `_` belongs to that engagement and is kept. A dialect without a server URL (where stage1 would exit 2), or whose server does not answer, is named in the record and the summary as not checked, with the reason, and purge goes on with the other dialect. It writes the destruction record {{p.records}}/destruction-record-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md (contracts records; Markdown): engagement, date, what was deleted (path, files and bytes per top-level directory of {{p.private}}), databases dropped (server, name), servers not checked, the source files with their sha256 from source.lock.json, and every entry of environment.windows_box.copies (path and what it is), to delete by hand; no file contents. It refuses (exit 2) when {{p.private}} is a symlink or does not end in /engagements/<id>/private. --dry-run prints the same plan as counts, sizes and database names, and deletes and writes nothing. The summary carries counts (files, bytes, databases), the database names and the servers not checked in messages (at most 50, contracts summary-schema; the record has the full list), and the destruction record in paths

toolkit/tests/test_report.py on hand-written fixtures in toolkit/tests/fixtures/report/ (an engagement.json with its paths.local.json; a manifest.json naming two seeds; equivalence JUnit files for engagement and the two seeds on two databases in one directory and app JUnit files with rule, e2e and other tests in a second directory; rules.json, known-differences.json, inventory.json and a test_rules.py): rate maths (lowest cell, pooled, coverage-adjusted); failed, error, skipped and not-implemented count as not passed; required cells follow the engagement's databases and the manifest's seeds; a missing required file exits 1; a file in both directories exits 2; an app file without e2e test cases gives no e2e cell; a cell whose total differs from the manifest exits 1; a canary string CANARY-1 in a failure message appears in neither results.json nor the report; a not-passed unit without an entry exits 1; an uncharacterized unit shows the manifest's reason; two runs give identical bytes; --check catches a one-line change. toolkit/tests/test_purge.py uses tmp_path and an injected fake database server per dialect: --dry-run deletes nothing; a real run deletes the private tree (a directory that is a mount point, with os.path.ismount patched, is emptied and kept), drops every name pattern on each server, keeps a database of another engagement whose db_name (from MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES) extends this one, keeps a name that matches only when _ is a wildcard (testxnorthwind_demo_s1 for db_name northwind_demo), skips a server that does not answer and a dialect without a URL and names them, lists the environment.windows_box.copies entries, and writes the destruction record; an unset MP_OTHER_DB_NAMES exits 2; a symlinked or wrongly named private path is refused

templates/docs/equivalence-report.md is the skeleton with the 8 headings and $-placeholders; it holds no engagement content. Its Coverage section carries one fixed sentence that report.py keeps for Access kinds and leaves out for xlsm: Access report layouts and report-level totals are proven by the S5 view tests (test_views.py), rule tests and end-to-end tests, not by goldens (the Access reference adapter's render_document raises NotImplementedError)

tasks.title: Audit before release
lenses: Claims audit: every number in docs/equivalence-report.md, the app README and (demo) the root README section traces to equivalence/results.json, goldens/manifest.json, analysis/rules.json or the inventory and matches it. The headline is the lowest cell rate over engagement and seeds 1-3 on every database in database.primary and database.verify_also, at least 0.90, with failed, error, skipped, xfail, xpass, not-implemented and missing tests counted as not passed and no -k in the run; pooled and coverage-adjusted rates are shown but never used as the headline. Rule and end-to-end tests are 100%. SQL Server is claimed only for cells that ran locally; target CI is called a cross-check only (if the target repo has a CI run for the S6 branch, `gh run view` shows its synthetic-seed jobs passed on both databases; for a client target repo run it as `mp-data gh {{p.records}}/engagement.json -- run view <run id>`). Every not-passed unit has a known-differences entry with a reason that fits the rules and the synthetic-seed behaviour. Nothing says 'identical', '100% equivalent' or more than the numbers show. Before pictures say they are reconstructed; after pictures and the walkthrough script use seed-1 only. Every unit not characterized on a dataset shows the status and reason that goldens/manifest.json gives it. The mp-data summary of the matrix re-run in S6.report's verify list gives the same lowest-cell and pooled rates as the gate block of results.json, and the results.json your verify list writes to {{p.private}}/review/<your slot>/ is byte-identical to the committed one. You may read that file and the app JUnit in {{p.private}}/synthetic/results/S6/; never open {{p.private}}/results/ or any other data-zone path

Release safety: NOTICE.md lists every runtime package from uv export with its licence, every THIRD_PARTY.md under app/ with its text (core/ for Jackcess, Apache-2.0; each area's, such as Chart.js 4.5.1, MIT, when vendored, whose recorded sha256 matches the vendored file), htmx 2 (0BSD) inside django-htmx, the Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server bundled by mssql-python (proprietary Microsoft licence), cookiecutter-django (BSD-3-Clause) and the source credit (demo: Northwind names and structure as Microsoft's with a trademark note and no licence; InvoiceGenerator's MIT text with 'Copyright (c) 2023 MaxineXiong'). A client repo has no open-source LICENSE and its README states client ownership; the demo LICENSE is MIT for our code only. Nothing from client or Microsoft material is in either repo: the guard passes, no tracked file has a forbidden extension, no SVG or PNG shows a value from the engagement dataset, and no document quotes VBA, SQL, expressions or macro text. Secrets appear only as reference names in docs/runbook.md and docs/deploy/. docs/data-retention.md and docs/access-and-ownership.md match the engagement's data_policy, care_plan, secrets and hosting, and the purge dry run lists what data-retention.md says (the Windows-box copies from environment.windows_box.copies among them), including the destruction record destruction-record-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md in the records. Demo: the walkthrough video stays in {{p.private}}/synthetic/media/walkthrough/ and is never committed; docs/legal-check.md classes every published path and lists the pre-flip checks exactly as the S6 demo gate runs them, and other engagements' sections of the root README and NOTICE are unchanged
